docs.title: GSNet
docs.text: Run GSNet in five minutes from the authors' checkpoint: the weights, a first picture, the same from Python and in the browser, a first number on the benchmark. Then the options of every slot: what fits where GSNet ships its components, and what was measured for each.

docs.title: Run GSNet in five minutes
docs.text: From the authors' checkpoint to grasps on a scene: on the command line, from Python or in a browser, then a first number on a part of the benchmark. Every command here is run by the test suite (by parsing it, on a toy detector, or on the files it needs); what each printed when it was measured is said under it, with the date, the commit and the machine. The numbers come from the method's metafile and five_minutes.json.

docs.title: 1. The weights
docs.text:
GraspPanda trained GSNet once (the reproduced rows of its README), but those weights are not published yet: trained on GraspNet-1Billion (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); whether and where these weights are published has not been decided. What you can download is the checkpoint released with the reference code:

  • File: minkuresunet_realsense.tar, from https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RfdpEM2y0x98rV28d7B2Dg8LLFKnBkfL/view?usp=sharing
  • Licence: academic, non-commercial (SJTU), as the reference repository; trained on GraspNet-1Billion (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
  • SHA-256: a0b9d85b300e40c76b66d092de62138d74757d6b7c2037f0d364f33960c54aa9

Convert it once, from the root of your GraspPanda checkout (the converter is a tool of the repository; it is not installed with the package):

python -m tools.convert_checkpoint minkuresunet_realsense.tar gsnet_realsense.pth \
    --source-format graspness-unofficial --camera realsense

It writes gsnet_realsense.pth: every tensor of the authors' file under the name of the module that plays its role here, no value changed, with a note of the file it came from. A tensor left over or missing stops the conversion with a report; nothing is ever loaded partially.

Before you use it. It loads strictly and runs, but it is far below the paper: its best-ranked grasps run into the scene, so use it with the collision filter. Its README says what is known.

docs.title: 2. Grasps on the example scene
docs.text:
grasppanda demo gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
    --weights gsnet_realsense.pth --example --collision-filter

--example is the synthetic table-top scene that ships with GraspPanda: no dataset and no download. The command prints the config and its hash, how the weights loaded (every tensor matched, none missing), the test pipeline, the cloud, how many grasps the model predicted and how many the collision filter left (the config's variant cd: ModelFreeCollisionFilter), and the ten best grasps. It writes into work_dirs/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e/demo/:

  • grasps.npy: the grasps that are left, (G, 17) float32 in the GraspNet layout, best first, camera frame, metres;
  • grasps.png and grasps.gif: the cloud with the 30 best grasps, still and swinging around the scene;
  • example/: the scene as files (depth.png, rgb.png, mask.png, intrinsics.txt).

Measured with the authors' released file, converted: 14.8 s for the whole command; 15,000 points to the model, sampled from 316,254 in the workspace; 1024 grasps predicted, 418 left after ModelFreeCollisionFilter (2026-10-15, commit 0ddca31, one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs).

Measured with the weights trained here (not published): 16.6 s for the whole command; 15,000 points to the model, sampled from 316,254 in the workspace; 1024 grasps predicted, 689 left after ModelFreeCollisionFilter (2026-10-15, commit ea6268b, one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs).

The scene files stand in for a camera. On your own depth image, as on these:

grasppanda demo gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
    --weights gsnet_realsense.pth \
    --depth work_dirs/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e/demo/example/depth.png \
    --intrinsics work_dirs/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e/demo/example/intrinsics.txt \
    --workspace -0.25 -0.2 0.35 0.25 0.2 0.8 \
    --collision-filter --out work_dirs/camera

GSNet was trained on clouds cropped around the objects; on a camera image, --workspace (a box in the camera frame, metres) or --mask does that crop. Units and frames, the depth scale and the intrinsics: Your own camera.

docs.title: 3. The same from Python
docs.text:
from grasppanda import GraspInferencer
from grasppanda.apis import example_scene

scene = example_scene()  # the scene of --example
inferencer = GraspInferencer(
    "gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e", "gsnet_realsense.pth"
)
grasps = inferencer(
    depth=scene.depth, intrinsics=scene.intrinsics,
    depth_scale=scene.depth_scale, mask=scene.mask,
    table_from_camera=scene.table_from_camera, collision_filter=True,
)
print(len(grasps), grasps.sort_by_score().to_graspnet_array()[:3])

It runs the demo's pipeline on the demo's input, so it returns the demo's 418 grasps (the test suite checks that the two give the same array, on a toy detector). mask= stands in for the segmentation the config crops the workspace with; on your camera, pass a mask from any segmentation or workspace=(xmin, ymin, zmin, xmax, ymax, zmax) in metres. The fields of a grasp and what else the call takes: From Python.

docs.title: 4. In the browser
docs.text:
# ~/grasppanda_weights: the folder that holds gsnet_realsense.pth
grasppanda explore --weights-dir ~/grasppanda_weights

The page opens at http://127.0.0.1:8765/. In the tab Run a method choose GSNet: gsnet_realsense.pth is chosen for you by its name. Keep the example scene (or upload a depth image with its intrinsics), tick the collision filter and press Run: the page shows the picture, the best ten grasps, the counts through the post-processing and the command that does the same in a terminal. The server listens on your machine only, reads weights only from that folder and downloads nothing: Run in the browser.

docs.title: 5. A first number on the benchmark
docs.text:
With GraspNet-1Billion on disk (export GRASPPANDA_GRASPNET1B_ROOT=..., see Dataset preparation), score the weights on every 64th frame of the seen test scenes, 120 frames:

grasppanda test gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
    --weights gsnet_realsense.pth \
    --opts data.test.dataset.split=test_seen data.test.dataset.frame_step=64 evaluation.num_workers=4

It prints AP, AP0.8 and AP0.4 for every variant of the config, raw (the predictions as they are) and cd (with the collision filter), and writes a result record per variant into the run directory under work_dirs/. Testing needs no derived asset; the evaluator extracts a cache from the dataset's object models the first time it runs, which the times below do not include.

Weights, provenance Collision filter AP, 120 frames of test_seen AP, whole seen split Difference Wall time, commit the authors' released file, converted, author-ckpt off 19.23 not scored on the whole split — 36.6 s, 0ddca31 on 39.75 not scored on the whole split — the weights trained here (not published), reproduced off 67.82 68.83 (record) −1.01 40 s, ea6268b on 70.74 71.23 (record) −0.49

Provenance: author-ckpt, the authors' weights, evaluated by GraspPanda; reproduced, trained and evaluated by GraspPanda. Inputs: the workspace is cropped around the ground-truth segmentation (gt_assisted: workspace), as in the reference. On these 120 frames the AP is within 1.01 AP of the whole split, so the subset tells you quickly whether your installation gives what the records say; it is not a benchmark number. Measured on 2026-10-15 on one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs.

The machine: one NVIDIA RTX A6000 (48 GB) shared with other jobs, an AMD EPYC 7262 with OMP_NUM_THREADS=3; Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.7.1 with CUDA 11.8, spconv 2.3.8.

docs.title: The options of every slot
docs.text:
Every slot of GSNet (gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e), what the method ships with there, the options that fit it and the ones that do not, each with what was measured: the cells of the measured grid that replace that one slot of GSNet. The method itself: its README. The same lists, with every message whole, in a terminal or as JSON:

grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list            # every slot
grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list <slot> --json

One run, seed 0, 20 iterations, 8 frames of one scene; a class counts verdicts, not accuracy. No accuracy appears on this page, and none follows from it: a probe trains 20 iterations on 8 frames and shows whether a combination works, not how good it is.

How to read a row: C R L P are the four levels of the cell under GSNet, composes, runs, learns and predicts (✓ reached, ✗ not, ? undecided: not checked for a record of the first judge, unstable, not repeated for an unstable run nobody probed again). The Class of an option counts the methods under which it reached each level; levels with the same class are named together. A probe that predicted no grasp on any frame is greyed. The levels, the classes and their thresholds are defined on the measured page, Measured classes.

docs.title: HGGD
docs.text: Run HGGD in five minutes from the authors' checkpoint: the weights, a first picture, the same from Python and in the browser, a first number on the benchmark. Then the options of every slot: what fits where HGGD ships its components, and what was measured for each.

docs.title: Run HGGD in five minutes
docs.text: From the authors' checkpoint to grasps on a scene: on the command line, from Python or in a browser, then a first number on a part of the benchmark. Every command here is run by the test suite (by parsing it, on a toy detector, or on the files it needs); what each printed when it was measured is said under it, with the date, the commit and the machine. The numbers come from the method's metafile and five_minutes.json.

docs.title: 1. The weights
docs.text:
GraspPanda publishes no weights for HGGD: the checkpoint is the authors', under their licence, and weights converted from it are not redistributed by the project. Download the authors' file yourself:

  • File: HGGD_realsense_checkpoint, from https://cloud.tsinghua.edu.cn/d/e3edfc2c8b114513b7eb/
  • Licence: MIT (the upstream repository); trained on GraspNet-1Billion (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
  • SHA-256: b95da06d8723298ad28e4c720c3a6a8af73dfe6f2e8126f43de8845bf62ad6df

Convert it once, from the root of your GraspPanda checkout (the converter is a tool of the repository; it is not installed with the package):

python -m tools.convert_checkpoint HGGD_realsense_checkpoint hggd_realsense.pth \
    --source-format hggd --camera realsense

It writes hggd_realsense.pth: every tensor of the authors' file under the name of the module that plays its role here, no value changed, with a note of the file it came from. A tensor left over or missing stops the conversion with a report; nothing is ever loaded partially.

docs.title: 2. Grasps on the example scene
docs.text:
grasppanda demo hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e \
    --weights hggd_realsense.pth --example --collision-filter

--example is the synthetic table-top scene that ships with GraspPanda: no dataset and no download. The command prints the config and its hash, how the weights loaded (every tensor matched, none missing), the test pipeline, the cloud, how many grasps the model predicted and how many the collision filter left (the config's variant cd: ModelFreeCollisionFilter then GraspNMS), and the ten best grasps. It writes into work_dirs/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e/demo/:

  • grasps.npy: the grasps that are left, (G, 17) float32 in the GraspNet layout, best first, camera frame, metres;
  • grasps.png and grasps.gif: the cloud with the 30 best grasps, still and swinging around the scene;
  • example/: the scene as files (depth.png, rgb.png, mask.png, intrinsics.txt).

Measured with the authors' checkpoint, converted: 14.5 s for the whole command; 25,600 points to the model; 470 grasps predicted, then 287 after ModelFreeCollisionFilter → 72 after GraspNMS (2026-10-15, commit ea6268b, one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs). Run again at commit 0ddca31 (2026-10-15): the same counts, 16.9 s.

The scene files stand in for a camera. On your own depth image, as on these:

grasppanda demo hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e \
    --weights hggd_realsense.pth \
    --depth work_dirs/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e/demo/example/depth.png \
    --intrinsics work_dirs/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e/demo/example/intrinsics.txt \
    --rgb work_dirs/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e/demo/example/rgb.png \
    --collision-filter --out work_dirs/camera

HGGD reads the colour image registered to the depth image (--rgb) and crops no workspace. Units and frames, the depth scale and the intrinsics: Your own camera.

docs.title: 3. The same from Python
docs.text:
from grasppanda import GraspInferencer
from grasppanda.apis import example_scene

scene = example_scene()  # the scene of --example
inferencer = GraspInferencer(
    "hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e", "hggd_realsense.pth"
)
grasps = inferencer(
    depth=scene.depth, intrinsics=scene.intrinsics,
    depth_scale=scene.depth_scale, rgb=scene.rgb, collision_filter=True,
)
print(len(grasps), grasps.sort_by_score().to_graspnet_array()[:3])

It runs the demo's pipeline on the demo's input, so it returns the demo's 72 grasps. Measured: 72 grasps, 8.2 s for the script (2026-10-15, commit 0ddca31, one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs). HGGD reads the colour image (rgb=) and takes no mask. The fields of a grasp and what else the call takes: From Python.

docs.title: 4. In the browser
docs.text:
# ~/grasppanda_weights: the folder that holds hggd_realsense.pth
grasppanda explore --weights-dir ~/grasppanda_weights

The page opens at http://127.0.0.1:8765/. In the tab Run a method choose HGGD: hggd_realsense.pth is chosen for you by its name. Keep the example scene (or upload a depth image with its intrinsics), tick the collision filter and press Run: the page shows the picture, the best ten grasps, the counts through the post-processing and the command that does the same in a terminal. The server listens on your machine only, reads weights only from that folder and downloads nothing: Run in the browser.

docs.title: 5. A first number on the benchmark
docs.text:
With GraspNet-1Billion on disk (export GRASPPANDA_GRASPNET1B_ROOT=..., see Dataset preparation), score the weights on every 64th frame of the seen test scenes, 120 frames:

grasppanda test hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e \
    --weights hggd_realsense.pth \
    --opts data.test.dataset.split=test_seen data.test.dataset.frame_step=64 evaluation.num_workers=4

It prints AP, AP0.8 and AP0.4 for every variant of the config, raw (the predictions as they are) and cd (with the collision filter), and writes a result record per variant into the run directory under work_dirs/. Testing needs no derived asset; the evaluator extracts a cache from the dataset's object models the first time it runs, which the times below do not include.

Weights, provenance Collision filter AP, 120 frames of test_seen AP, whole seen split Difference Wall time, commit the authors' checkpoint, converted, author-ckpt off 58.16 58.33 (record) −0.17 53 s, ea6268b on 64.14 63.70 (record) +0.44

Provenance: author-ckpt, the authors' weights, evaluated by GraspPanda. Inputs: no input is derived from ground truth (the config crops no workspace). On these 120 frames the AP is within 0.44 AP of the whole split, so the subset tells you quickly whether your installation gives what the records say; it is not a benchmark number. Measured on 2026-10-15 on one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs.

The machine: one NVIDIA RTX A6000 (48 GB) shared with other jobs, an AMD EPYC 7262 with OMP_NUM_THREADS=3; Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.7.1 with CUDA 11.8, spconv 2.3.8.

docs.text:
Every slot of HGGD (hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e), what the method ships with there, the options that fit it and the ones that do not, each with what was measured: the cells of the measured grid that replace that one slot of HGGD. The method itself: its README. The same lists, with every message whole, in a terminal or as JSON:

grasppanda compose hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e --list            # every slot
grasppanda compose hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e --list <slot> --json

One run, seed 0, 20 iterations, 8 frames of one scene; a class counts verdicts, not accuracy. No accuracy appears on this page, and none follows from it: a probe trains 20 iterations on 8 frames and shows whether a combination works, not how good it is.

How to read a row: C R L P are the four levels of the cell under HGGD, composes, runs, learns and predicts (✓ reached, ✗ not, ? undecided: not checked for a record of the first judge, unstable, not repeated for an unstable run nobody probed again). The Class of an option counts the methods under which it reached each level; levels with the same class are named together. A probe that predicted no grasp on any frame is greyed. The levels, the classes and their thresholds are defined on the measured page, Measured classes.

docs.title: Scale-Balanced-Grasp
docs.text: Run Scale-Balanced-Grasp in five minutes from the authors' checkpoint: the weights, a first picture, the same from Python and in the browser, a first number on the benchmark. Then the options of every slot: what fits where Scale-Balanced-Grasp ships its components, and what was measured for each.

docs.title: Run Scale-Balanced-Grasp in five minutes
docs.text: From the authors' checkpoint to grasps on a scene: on the command line, from Python or in a browser, then a first number on a part of the benchmark. Every command here is run by the test suite (by parsing it, on a toy detector, or on the files it needs); what each printed when it was measured is said under it, with the date, the commit and the machine. The numbers come from the method's metafile and five_minutes.json.

docs.title: 1. The weights
docs.text:
GraspPanda publishes no weights for Scale-Balanced-Grasp: the checkpoint is the authors', under their licence, and weights converted from it are not redistributed by the project. Download the authors' file yourself:

  • File: checkpoint-rs.tar, from https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Y2o0uAbhS6-yZhPkKMAAnL0tCpbiJfk0?usp=share_link
  • Licence: as the upstream repository (MIT file; derived from non-commercial code)
  • SHA-256: ebf63c146a7dfd8ced4543b9b9e5b9506cff320bb4b8157cab0c78b3e6ce5aef

Convert it once, from the root of your GraspPanda checkout (the converter is a tool of the repository; it is not installed with the package):

python -m tools.convert_checkpoint checkpoint-rs.tar sbg_realsense.pth \
    --source-format scale-balanced-grasp --camera realsense

It writes sbg_realsense.pth: every tensor of the authors' file under the name of the module that plays its role here, no value changed, with a note of the file it came from. A tensor left over or missing stops the conversion with a report; nothing is ever loaded partially.

docs.title: 2. Grasps on the example scene
docs.text:
grasppanda demo scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e \
    --weights sbg_realsense.pth --example --collision-filter

--example is the synthetic table-top scene that ships with GraspPanda: no dataset and no download. The command prints the config and its hash, how the weights loaded (every tensor matched, none missing), the test pipeline, the cloud, how many grasps the model predicted and how many the collision filter left (the config's variant cd: ModelFreeCollisionFilter), and the ten best grasps. It writes into work_dirs/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e/demo/:

  • grasps.npy: the grasps that are left, (G, 17) float32 in the GraspNet layout, best first, camera frame, metres;
  • grasps.png and grasps.gif: the cloud with the 30 best grasps, still and swinging around the scene;
  • example/: the scene as files (depth.png, rgb.png, mask.png, intrinsics.txt).

Measured with the authors' checkpoint, converted: 10.5 s for the whole command; 20,000 points to the model, sampled from 316,254 in the workspace; 262 grasps predicted, 189 left after ModelFreeCollisionFilter (2026-10-15, commit ea6268b, one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs).

The scene files stand in for a camera. On your own depth image, as on these:

grasppanda demo scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e \
    --weights sbg_realsense.pth \
    --depth work_dirs/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e/demo/example/depth.png \
    --intrinsics work_dirs/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e/demo/example/intrinsics.txt \
    --workspace -0.25 -0.2 0.35 0.25 0.2 0.8 \
    --collision-filter --out work_dirs/camera

Scale-Balanced-Grasp was trained on clouds cropped around the objects; on a camera image, --workspace (a box in the camera frame, metres) or --mask does that crop. Units and frames, the depth scale and the intrinsics: Your own camera.

docs.title: 3. The same from Python
docs.text:
from grasppanda import GraspInferencer
from grasppanda.apis import example_scene

scene = example_scene()  # the scene of --example
inferencer = GraspInferencer(
    "scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e", "sbg_realsense.pth"
)
grasps = inferencer(
    depth=scene.depth, intrinsics=scene.intrinsics,
    depth_scale=scene.depth_scale, mask=scene.mask,
    table_from_camera=scene.table_from_camera, collision_filter=True,
)
print(len(grasps), grasps.sort_by_score().to_graspnet_array()[:3])

It runs the demo's pipeline on the demo's input, so it returns the demo's 189 grasps (the test suite checks that the two give the same array, on a toy detector). mask= stands in for the segmentation the config crops the workspace with; on your camera, pass a mask from any segmentation or workspace=(xmin, ymin, zmin, xmax, ymax, zmax) in metres. The fields of a grasp and what else the call takes: From Python.

docs.title: 4. In the browser
docs.text:
# ~/grasppanda_weights: the folder that holds sbg_realsense.pth
grasppanda explore --weights-dir ~/grasppanda_weights

The page opens at http://127.0.0.1:8765/. In the tab Run a method choose Scale-Balanced-Grasp: sbg_realsense.pth is chosen for you by its name. Keep the example scene (or upload a depth image with its intrinsics), tick the collision filter and press Run: the page shows the picture, the best ten grasps, the counts through the post-processing and the command that does the same in a terminal. The server listens on your machine only, reads weights only from that folder and downloads nothing: Run in the browser.

docs.title: 5. A first number on the benchmark
docs.text:
With GraspNet-1Billion on disk (export GRASPPANDA_GRASPNET1B_ROOT=..., see Dataset preparation), score the weights on every 64th frame of the seen test scenes, 120 frames:

grasppanda test scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e \
    --weights sbg_realsense.pth \
    --opts data.test.dataset.split=test_seen data.test.dataset.frame_step=64 evaluation.num_workers=4

It prints AP, AP0.8 and AP0.4 for every variant of the config, raw (the predictions as they are) and cd (with the collision filter), and writes a result record per variant into the run directory under work_dirs/. Testing needs no derived asset; the evaluator extracts a cache from the dataset's object models the first time it runs, which the times below do not include.

Weights, provenance Collision filter AP, 120 frames of test_seen AP, whole seen split Difference Wall time, commit the authors' checkpoint, converted, author-ckpt off 57.87 57.78 (record) +0.09 37 s, ea6268b on 62.84 62.29 (record) +0.55

Provenance: author-ckpt, the authors' weights, evaluated by GraspPanda. Inputs: the workspace is cropped around the ground-truth segmentation (gt_assisted: workspace), as in the reference. On these 120 frames the AP is within 0.55 AP of the whole split, so the subset tells you quickly whether your installation gives what the records say; it is not a benchmark number. Measured on 2026-10-15 on one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs.

The machine: one NVIDIA RTX A6000 (48 GB) shared with other jobs, an AMD EPYC 7262 with OMP_NUM_THREADS=3; Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.7.1 with CUDA 11.8, spconv 2.3.8.

docs.title: The options of every slot
docs.text:
Every slot of Scale-Balanced-Grasp (scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e), what the method ships with there, the options that fit it and the ones that do not, each with what was measured: the cells of the measured grid that replace that one slot of Scale-Balanced-Grasp. The method itself: its README. The same lists, with every message whole, in a terminal or as JSON:

grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e --list            # every slot
grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e --list <slot> --json

One run, seed 0, 20 iterations, 8 frames of one scene; a class counts verdicts, not accuracy. No accuracy appears on this page, and none follows from it: a probe trains 20 iterations on 8 frames and shows whether a combination works, not how good it is.

How to read a row: C R L P are the four levels of the cell under Scale-Balanced-Grasp, composes, runs, learns and predicts (✓ reached, ✗ not, ? undecided: not checked for a record of the first judge, unstable, not repeated for an unstable run nobody probed again). The Class of an option counts the methods under which it reached each level; levels with the same class are named together. A probe that predicted no grasp on any frame is greyed. The levels, the classes and their thresholds are defined on the measured page, Measured classes.

docs.title: Slots: the stages of the pipeline and what can go into each
docs.text:
GraspPanda builds a grasp detector from stages, and every stage is a slot of the config: a place where one component can be replaced by another that keeps the same contract. This page is the map: the pipeline, the task of every slot, its 248 options in all, and which option was measured to work under which method. Every slot has a page of its own with one row and one command per option.

No accuracy is claimed for any option that is not one of the six ported methods. An option is listed because it was built, trained for 20 iterations on 8 real frames of GraspNet-1Billion and asked to predict (grasppanda probe). That shows it is usable, not that it is good; the model zoo is still empty.

To try options without reading further, open the combination explorer: pick a method, change a slot, read the measured verdict and the command.

docs.title: Words used on these pages
docs.text:
• seed: a point of the scene at which a grasp is predicted; the proposal picks the seeds (1024 per frame in the ported methods).
  • contract: what a component declares about its input and output (where its features live, which axes a tensor has, which labels it reads). The config check compares contracts before anything is built and refuses a mismatch with the fix.
  • preset: a small YAML file with a component and settings for table-top depth clouds; the name after --set <slot>=.
  • adapter: a wrapper compose puts around a scene encoder so that it fits the next stage (features propagated back to every point, or kept on a subsample).
  • dense / compact label set: the grasp labels a head is trained on. Dense is the full grid of GraspNet-1Billion (300 views × 12 in-plane angles × 4 depths per labelled point); compact keeps the best grasp per view (EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp). A head, its assigner and the dataset section must use the same one.
  • point painting: giving every point the image feature at its pixel, which is how a seed-based method reads an image encoder.

docs.title: The pipeline
docs.text:
observation: a depth image as a point cloud (HGGD also reads the colour image)
  │
  ├─ the seed-based methods
  │    scene encoder ─► seed proposal ─► view ─► (assigner) ─► grouper ─► head bundle ─┐
  │    features         seeds            approach  labels,       crops                 │
  │                                                training                            │
  └─ HGGD: image encoder ─► heat-map and region stages (no slots of their own yet) ────┤
  grasps for the evaluator or a robot ◄─ post-processing ◄─ GraspGroup ◄───────────────┘

around the model: the loss of every stage · the training recipe

Six methods are ported. Five share the seed-based skeleton and therefore its six stage slots (GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp, GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp); HGGD is a detector family of its own with one slot so far, the image encoder. Losses, post-processing and the training recipe are around the stages and apply to all six.

docs.title: The slots
docs.text:
An option is a name you can write after --set <slot>=: a preset (a component with settings for table-top depth clouds) or a component with its defaults.

The assigner has no page of its own: it goes with the head bundle and the label set (Heads and losses, Data contracts). The scene encoders have an overview and three pages: point-based networks, sparse-voxel networks and released weights, transformers and pretrained 3-D encoders. The encoders ported before these pages are in Scene encoders of the model zoo.

docs.title: Which option fits which method
docs.text:
From the measured records (1262 recorded cells: 1014 runs, 174 runs-empty, 29 runs-unstable, 41 refused, 4 fails), with one slot replaced at a time. Every method has a page that lists the options of each of its slots with what was measured for each, and so does grasppanda compose <method config> --list <slot>: GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp, GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp, HGGD.

One run, seed 0, 20 iterations, 8 frames of one scene; a class counts verdicts, not accuracy. A cell (one option under one method) is decided at four levels, each from its record alone; every level needs the one before it:

  • composes: the contract rules and the config check accept the composed config: grasppanda compose writes it (any verdict but refused). A refusal by policy is undecided (needs consent), and so is a request that is not a combination.
  • runs: the probe ran clean on real frames: the verdict runs or runs-empty. A runs-unstable probe counts as not running only when its repeat (repeat in the record: the same config, seed and schedule) was unstable too; without a repeat the level is undecided (unstable, not repeated); when the repeat ran clean the cell runs, and learns and predicts are read from the repeat. fails does not run.
  • learns: judge 2 only. Every loss term was active (reported, finite, not exactly 0) in at least 50 % of the iterations and fell by at least 5 % (fall = (first - mean of the last quarter) / |first| over its active iterations), and no term is flagged flat, rising or constant; a term that is 0 at the last iteration (zero_at_end) is judged on its active iterations. Every unit with trainable parameters received a gradient (no_gradient is empty) and every part changed (unchanged is empty).
  • predicts: judge 2 only. Every predicted frame has at least one grasp, and on every frame the smallest and the largest score differ (score_quantiles): a model whose scores collapsed to one value ranks nothing.

A level that cannot be decided from a record says why:

  • not checked: the record was judged by the first judge, which recorded neither the trend of the loss terms nor the scores of the predicted grasps.
  • unstable, not repeated: the probe was runs-unstable and has not been repeated: an unstable run counts as not running only when a second probe of the same config is unstable too.
  • needs consent: refused by a policy that waits for the user's consent (trust_remote_code needs accept_remote_code: true): a rule about this machine, not about the combination.
  • not a combination: the request names a component that lacks an option only a preset supplies: it is refused before any contract is compared, and is no combination.
  • not probed: the grid has the cell, but no record yet.
  • not reached by the method as shipped: the method as shipped, probed the same way, does not reach this level either (for example FineGrasp at the constant rate, whose fusion of crop scales gives every seed one feature in a short run, so every grasp gets one score): under that method the level says nothing about the option at this budget.

The class of an option at a level counts the methods under which it reached that level. For a stage of the seed-based skeleton decided under all five seed-based methods (GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp, GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp):

  • universal: it reached the level under all five seed-based methods.
  • most: under three or four of them.
  • some: under two.
  • specific: under exactly one.
  • none: under none of them.

An option of another slot (post-processing, loss, recipe, image encoder) is universal only when it reached the level under every method it applies to and those include the five seed-based ones. Every other class reads N of M probed: it reached the level under N of the M methods where the level was decided, and the methods where it was not are named after it (+2 not checked). A level that no method decided is named by the reason. A level decided only where the level before it failed is not checked: the class says so instead of counting the failures again.

† The slot was not probed under the five seed-based methods but under the methods of the second column, so its classes count those. (defaults): the component named by its type and built with its constructor defaults, not a preset; a component that needs an option only a preset supplies does not work that way.   • target-mask has no cell of its own: reads observation.masks, which no shipped dataset fills.
  • distribution-focal has no cell of its own: fits bins terms only, which no shipped method has; probed as the width loss of the head preset decoupled-grid-bins (stage cells).
  • DepthEmbedGroup (grouper) has no cell under its type name: it needs an option only a preset supplies; its presets are classified.
  • DepthPoolGroup (grouper) has no cell under its type name: it needs an option only a preset supplies; its presets are classified.
  • MultiRadiusGroup (grouper) has no cell under its type name: it needs an option only a preset supplies; its presets are classified.
  • MultiScaleGroup (grouper) has no cell under its type name: it needs an option only a preset supplies; its presets are classified.

How to read it:

  • A class is not a ranking. universal at a level says that a swap reached that level under every method without anything else changed; it says nothing about accuracy.
  • An option that is not universal is usually bound to its neighbours, not to a paper. A head bundle goes with the assigner and the label set it is supervised with, a grouper with the axes its head reads, a scoring proposal with the stage that owns objectness. Replaced together with what they depend on they run under other methods too: see Sets of stages and Several slots at once.
  • A refusal comes with the fix. grasppanda compose prints the contract that is violated and the option or preset that satisfies it, before anything is built.
  • A loss or a recipe preset with a class N of M probed below M did not run everywhere it was put: the loss and recipe pages say where and why (a term of another kind, a detector that reads images, mixed precision).
  • What was not probed is not classified. Most combinations of two or more options have no record; the explorer shows for any two options what the config check answers, which is a weaker statement than a probe.

docs.title: How to try one
docs.text:
grasppanda compose --list grouper                                # the presets of a slot
grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list grouper
                                                                 # ... under GSNet, measured
grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
    --set grouper=roi-grid -o gsnet_roi-grid.yaml                 # a checked config
grasppanda probe gsnet_roi-grid.yaml                             # 20 iterations on
                                                                 # real frames: runs?
grasppanda train gsnet_roi-grid.yaml                             # the real run
  • Several --set go into one command (--set backbone=point-transformer-v2 --set grouper=cylinder-vector-attention, a recorded combination); compose inserts the adapter the contracts ask for and says so, or refuses with the conflict and the fix.
  • grasppanda compose --show grouper=roi-grid prints one preset with what must be re-tuned; grasppanda components --slot groupers prints the contracts, sources and optional libraries of every component.
  • grasppanda explore serves the explorer locally and checks any selection with the compose of your installation.
  • probe needs GraspNet-1Billion and the label assets of the method (Try a combination lists the prepare commands). An option that is a bridge to a library names the extra to install on its slot page. Until the first release on PyPI, install an extra from the repository root with pip install -e ".[<extra>]": the form pip install "grasppanda[<extra>]" resolves against the metadata of the copy that is already installed and may install nothing.
  • Under Scale-Balanced-Grasp a probe ends as wired (a synthetic scene, exit status 3) unless it is given the reference's width histogram: grasppanda probe <config> --opts data.train.dataset.scale_statistic.source=legacy_import data.train.dataset.scale_statistic.reference_sha256=<SHA-256>. The histogram is a statistic of a whole training split and cannot be built from the eight frames of a probe (configs/scale_balanced_grasp/README.md says how to import the file); the recorded runs of that method were measured this way.
  • grasppanda compose --list image_encoder lists the image encoders (the slot of HGGD); the seed-based methods read one through point painting.

docs.title: Grouper: what is gathered around a seed and how it becomes the feature the head reads
docs.text:
Words such as seed, contract, preset, adapter, label set and point painting are explained in the slot index.

Which of these options fit a method

Every method has a page that lists the options of each of its slots with what was measured for each (the verdict, the levels composes, runs, learns and predicts, the class, the grasps, the reason of a refusal): GSNet (grouper); EconomicGrasp (grouper); FineGrasp (grouper); GraspNet-baseline (grouper); Scale-Balanced-Grasp (grouper). In a terminal: grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list grouper.

Class: one run, seed 0, 20 iterations, 8 frames of one scene; a class counts verdicts, not accuracy. Where this page names a class or a measured verdict, it is one of the measured classes.

docs.title: 1. The task of the slot
docs.text:
A seed-based detector (GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp, GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp) first picks about a thousand seeds on the scene and one approach direction per seed. The grouper then looks at the neighbourhood of every seed in the frame of that approach direction and turns it into one feature vector (or one per insertion depth). The head bundle predicts in-plane angle, depth, width and score from that feature and nothing else, so the grouper decides what the head can know about the local shape.

Position in the pipeline: backbone → proposal → view → (assigner) → grouper → head.

Every published crop is the same five steps, and almost every alternative replaces exactly one of them:

step what the ported methods do what this page adds query: which points, in which shape a cylinder along the approach axis ball, k nearest, oriented box, grid of balls, grid of cells geometry of a neighbour offset in the crop frame the same with its length encoder per neighbour shared MLP (plus self-attention in EconomicGrasp) DGCNN edge feature, PointNeXt InvResMLP, layers of PyTorch Geometric pooling maximum mean, attentive pooling, vector attention, all with a padding mask fusion, residual attention over radii (FineGrasp), linear + gate (Scale-Balanced-Grasp) linear / max / mean over radii (MultiRadiusGroup), projected seed residual

No AP is claimed for any option on this page. Each was built, trained for 20 iterations on 8 real frames and asked to predict (grasppanda probe); that shows it is usable, not that it is good.

docs.title: 2. Input and output
docs.text:
class Grouper(nn.Module):
    support: ClassVar[Literal["seeds", "scene"]]   # which points are grouped
    out_axes: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]]            # ("seed", "channel") or ("seed", "depth", "channel")
    out_channels: int                              # width of the returned feature
    uses_seed_features: bool = False               # forward takes the seed features as 4th argument

    def forward(self, support: PointFeatures, centres: Tensor, rotation: Tensor
                [, seed_feats: Tensor]) -> GroupFeatures: ...
support PointFeatures: points (N, 3) in metres, camera frame, with batch offsets, and features (N, C). With support = "seeds" these are the M seeds of the batch with the encoder's features (C = in_channels, the width of the scene encoder, injected by the detector). With support = "scene" it is the whole scene cloud (20 000 points per frame in the shipped recipes): with features under a dense encoder, with zero feature channels under a sub-sampling encoder. centres (M, 3) crop centre per seed, metres, camera frame. At inference the seed itself; in training the centre the assigner chose (the matched label point for some methods), so a crop may contain no point at all. rotation (M, 3, 3) crop frame per seed. Column 0 is the approach axis; the head counts in-plane angles about it from column 1. In training the frame comes from the labels and may be a reflection: a grouper must not assume a right-handed frame. A neighbour p sits at Rᵀ (p − c) in the crop frame. seed_feats (M, C) features of the seeds; passed only when the grouper sets uses_seed_features. returns GroupFeatures(feats, axes): (M, out_channels) with axes ("seed", "channel"), or (M, D, out_channels) with ("seed", "depth", "channel"), one row per seed in the order given.

All seeds of a batch are flattened: M = batch × seeds per frame, every frame has the same number of seeds, and a crop never sees points of another frame.

What the neighbours require, and what the config checker does with the contract attributes (stage_contract_problems in grasppanda/models/detectors/seed_based.py):

  • out_axes must equal the head's in_axes. SWADHead (GSNet) and EconomicHead (EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp) read ("seed", "channel"); OperationHead (GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp) reads ("seed", "depth", "channel"). An axis is never added or squeezed implicitly; the two adapters of section 4.6 do it explicitly.
  • The depth axis has one entry per depth bin of the head: the length of the grouper's hmax list, or its num_depth, must equal head.num_depth.
  • out_channels is handed to the head as its in_channels; nothing to configure.
  • The width of the seed features (new, see section 5): a grouper that adds the seed features to its crops states the width it needs (required_seed_channels), and the check compares it with what the encoder returns.
  • support must be seeds or scene. A scene-support grouper works under both kinds of encoder; whether it reads scene features is its own option.

Conventions of the queries (grasppanda.ops.ball_query, box_query, cylinder_query, knn): the first nsample hits in index order; missing slots repeat the first hit; a query without any hit returns point 0 of its frame. A maximum does not notice the copies; a mean or an attention does, which is why the groupers below mask them.

Route: own = written here on grasppanda.ops from the paper (a few lines per part), A = adapted source, L = bridge to a library. All weights are random init: no released checkpoint contains any of these crops for grasping. Venues are those of the arXiv record or the proceedings page, opened on 2026-10-13.

Universal or method-specific: every (seed, channel) option fits GSNet, EconomicGrasp and FineGrasp, because their heads read the same axes and the crop is the only thing that changes; every (seed, depth, channel) option fits GraspNet-baseline and Scale-Balanced-Grasp for the same reason. Through depth-embed and depth-pool each crop reaches the other family as well. voxel-set-abstraction, depth-* and depth-pool gather from the scene cloud and therefore do not depend on how densely the proposal places seeds.

docs.title: 4. How to use each option
docs.text:
One command composes a child config of a method with the grouper replaced, checks it, and says what it did; one more probes it on real frames:

grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --set grouper=roi-grid -o my.yaml
grasppanda probe my.yaml --iters 20 --frames 8
grasppanda train my.yaml

slot      component             from
────────  ────────────────────  ─────────────────
backbone  SparseUNet14          base config
proposal  GraspnessFPS          base config
view      TemplateViewStage     base config
assigner  NearestLabelAssigner  base config
grouper   RoIGridGroup          preset `roi-grid`
head      SWADHead              base config

contracts
  ✓ backbone · proposal
  ✓ backbone · grouper
  ...
  ✓ grouper · head

config check
  ✓ valid  (hash d99e1d7a282f)

An option of the grouper is changed on the same command line (--opts model.grouper.nsample=32) or in the file. Every preset is a file under grasppanda/presets/grouper/ whose header says what must be re-tuned. There are no pretrained weights to load for any grouper. To start the other stages from a checkpoint of the method with its own grouper, the options are runtime.load_from=<file> with runtime.allow_weight_mismatch=true (the keys that did not match are printed); this was not run for this page.

docs.title: 4.1 LocalGroup: shape, encoder and pooling as options
docs.text:
model:
  grouper:
    type: LocalGroup
    shape: cylinder          # ball | knn | box | cylinder
    radius: 0.05             # ball / cylinder radius, half side of the box section (m)
    hmin: -0.02              # box and cylinder: near and far end along the approach axis (m)
    hmax: 0.04
    nsample: 16              # neighbours per crop (k of knn)
    padding: first           # first: repeat the first member, masked | cyclic: repeat in turn
    geometry: offset         # offset | offset+distance
    encoder: mlp             # mlp | edge | invres
    pool: max                # max | mean | attentive | vector_attention
    mlp_channels: [256, 256] # the last width goes to the head

All 48 combinations of shape × encoder × pool are legal and unit-tested. How to choose:

  • shape: cylinder is what every grasp method uses (long along the approach axis). ball has no preferred axis. box is the cylinder with a square section, the shape of detection RoIs. knn has no radius: the reach follows the seed density, which helps on sparse regions and hurts when the 16 nearest seeds are all on the table.
  • encoder: edge tells the MLP how a neighbour differs from the seed (DOGraspNet reports this offset-driven aggregation for grasping; its code is non-commercial and was not used). invres adds capacity after the pooling and a residual path from the seed.
  • pool: max is robust to padding. mean, attentive and vector_attention use the padding mask. vector_attention is the only pooling that reads the seed's own feature.
  • The crop gathers among the seeds (1024 per frame): sizes and nsample belong to the seed density of the proposal as much as to the objects.

docs.title: 4.2 DepthLocalGroup: the same, over the scene, one feature per depth bin
docs.text:
model:
  grouper:
    type: DepthLocalGroup
    shape: ball                        # ball | knn | box | cylinder
    radius: 0.05
    hmin: -0.02
    hmax: [0.01, 0.02, 0.03, 0.04]     # one far end per depth bin of the head
    nsample: 64
    pool: max                          # max | mean | attentive
    mlp_channels: [64, 128, 256]
    seed_residual: none                # none | projected (adds W·f of the seed feature)

The crop is gathered once, to the farthest reach, and bin d pools the members with hmin < x < hmax[d]. This differs from DepthCylinderGroup, which queries nsample points per depth: here the near bins hold fewer members than nsample. seed_residual: projected works with any encoder width; the gated residual of Scale-Balanced-Grasp does not (section 5).

docs.title: 4.3 RoI pooling of 3-D detectors: RoIGridGroup, RoIAwareGroup, VoxelSetAbstractionGroup
docs.text:
grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --set grouper=roi-grid
grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --set grouper=roi-aware
grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --set grouper=voxel-set-abstraction

model:
  grouper:
    type: RoIGridGroup
    radius: 0.05          # the box: 2 * radius across the approach axis,
    hmin: -0.02           # hmin .. hmax along it
    hmax: 0.04
    grid_size: 3          # 27 grid points
    pool_radius: 0.03     # ball around every grid point; >= box side / grid_size
    nsample: 8
    mlp_channels: [64, 64]
    fc_channels: [256, 256]

The region of a detection RoI is a box with a yaw angle; here it is the box of a seed in its approach frame. Unlike a max over the crop, both RoI poolings keep where in the box a feature was found. roi-aware leaves empty cells at zero, so with 1024 seeds per frame most of its 64 cells are empty: try grid_size: 2 or 3. voxel-set-abstraction is the one option that reads the scene and returns (seed, channel); scene_features: true adds the dense features of the scene points and needs a dense encoder (otherwise the grouper stops with a message that says so).

docs.title: 4.4 PyGConvGroup: layers of PyTorch Geometric
docs.text:
pip install -e ".[torch_geometric]"        # torch_geometric, a pure Python wheel
grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --set grouper=pyg-gatv2-conv \
    --opts 'model.grouper.conv_args={heads: 8}'

model:
  grouper:
    type: PyGConvGroup
    conv: PointTransformerConv   # PointNetConv | PointTransformerConv | EdgeConv | GATv2Conv | TransformerConv
    conv_args: {}                # further keyword arguments of the layer
    shape: cylinder              # the same shapes as LocalGroup
    radius: 0.05
    hmin: -0.02
    hmax: 0.04
    nsample: 16
    out_channels: 256

The crop is handed to the layer as a bipartite graph in the crop frame: every member is a source node at its offset Rᵀ (p − c) / radius, the seed is the target node at the origin. Nothing is padded: a crop with five members has five edges. The five layers above are the ones that were run; adding another needs three lines in PYG_CONVS (grasppanda/models/groupers/pyg.py).

docs.title: 4.5 Several radii: MultiRadiusGroup (linear, max, mean) and MultiScaleGroup (attention)
docs.text:
grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --set grouper=multi-scale-linear

model:
  grouper:
    type: MultiRadiusGroup
    radius: 0.07                       # largest crop
    radius_scales: [0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0]
    fusion: linear                     # linear | max | mean
    branch:                            # one copy per radius; its radius is set above
      type: CylinderGroup
      nsample: 16
      mlp_channels: [256, 256]

branch is any seeds-support grouper with a radius, LocalGroup and PyGConvGroup included. MultiScaleGroup (preset multi-scale) is the same with FineGrasp's attention over the scales.

docs.title: 4.6 The other family's crops: depth-embed and depth-pool
docs.text:
# a (seed, channel) crop under GraspNet-baseline or Scale-Balanced-Grasp
grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e \
    --set grouper=depth-embed
# a depth-sliced scene crop under GSNet, EconomicGrasp or FineGrasp
grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --set grouper=depth-pool

model:
  grouper:
    type: DepthEmbedGroup
    num_depth: 4                 # = model.head.num_depth
    grouper: {type: RoIGridGroup}   # any seeds-support (seed, channel) grouper

depth-embed computes the crop once and tells the depth bins apart only by a learned embedding, which is weaker than a crop per depth; depth-pool throws the depth resolution away. They exist so that a swap is possible, not because a paper proposes them.

docs.title: 5. The width of the seed features
docs.text:
Scale-Balanced-Grasp's crop adds sigmoid(W f) · f of the seed feature f to its 256-channel crop features, so the encoder had to return 256 channels. An encoder with an out_channels option was fitted by compose; one without (LitePT, PTv3 and its pretrained variants, PointNeXt, PointNet2Dense) passed the config check and failed when the model was built. Now:

  • DepthCylinderGroup.required_seed_channels(options) states the width, and the config check compares it with the width the encoder declares for its options (Backbone.output_channels; an encoder whose width is known only once built, such as Uni3D without out_channels, is built once for the check, without released weights). grasppanda compose ... --set backbone=PointNeXt --no-adapter under Scale-Balanced-Grasp now ends with:
✗ backbone · grouper: DepthCylinderGroup as configured adds the seed features to its
  256-channel crop features, but PointNeXt returns 32-channel features. Use
  `type: DepthCylinderProjectionGroup` for the grouper (the same crop with a linear layer
  in front of the residual; `grasppanda compose` does that), or give the encoder 256
  output channels where it has that option, or end the grouper's `mlp_channels` on 32, or
  set `seed_residual: none`.
  • DepthCylinderProjectionGroup is the same crop with a linear layer in_channels → out_channels in front of the gate. Without --no-adapter, compose puts it in place of DepthCylinderGroup, with the options of the crop it replaces, and says so:
grouper   DepthCylinderProjectionGroup         base config, projected
...
• grouper: DepthCylinderProjectionGroup in place of DepthCylinderGroup. DepthCylinderGroup as
  configured adds the seed features to its 256-channel crop features, but FurthestPointSubsample
  returns 32-channel features. DepthCylinderProjectionGroup is the same crop with a linear layer
  in front of its seed residual; it changes the model (the base method has none). `--no-adapter`
  leaves the pair refused.

The reference model has no such layer, so the composed model is a variant of Scale-Balanced-Grasp, not the paper's.

  • The fix is a class of its own, not an option of DepthCylinderGroup, on purpose: the config hash of a shipped config covers the constructor defaults of its components, so a new option on a ported class would change the hash of every config that uses it (and orphan their measured records and checkpoints). The same holds for MultiRadiusGroup beside MultiScaleGroup.

The same holds for every encoder preset without a 256-channel output, including those that start from released weights (the check learns the width from the architecture, so its verdict does not depend on which weight files are on the machine). The encoder cells under Scale-Balanced-Grasp that used to fail at build were probed again; in each, compose put DepthCylinderProjectionGroup in place of DepthCylinderGroup:

docs.title: 6. Pitfalls met while building this
docs.text:
• Padding and non-max pooling. The queries repeat the first hit in empty slots. With a mean or an attention those copies would outvote the real members; LocalGroup, DepthLocalGroup and VoxelSetAbstractionGroup mask them, and PyGConvGroup does not create them. If you write a pooling of your own, use the mask crop_members returns.
  • Empty crops in training. The crop centre comes from the assigner and need not be a seed, so a seed-support box or cylinder may be empty. The queries then return point 0 of the frame; here its first slot counts as the only member, so no pooling reduces an empty set (a soft-max over nothing is NaN).
  • Do not add an option to a component that shipped configs use. The first version of this work added fusion to MultiScaleGroup and seed_projection to DepthCylinderGroup; 130 measured cells stopped matching what compose writes, because the config hash had changed. New behaviour goes into a new class or a subclass.
  • A bridge passes the config check without its library. The check compares contracts and does not build; PyGConvGroup without torch_geometric stops when the model is built, with the pip install line.
  • Scale-Balanced-Grasp needs its width histogram to be probed on real frames (data.train.dataset.scale_statistic); without it grasppanda probe falls back to a synthetic scene and reports wired. tools/probe_grid.py takes --scale-statistic-sha for that.
  • knn over the scene is short-sighted. With 20 000 points the 64 nearest lie within about a centimetre, so the far depth bins of depth-knn see the same members as the near ones. Raise nsample or prefer a radius.
  • Memory. A scene-support crop holds seeds × nsample × width activations per MLP layer (and per depth for DepthCylinderGroup); two probes side by side on a shared GPU can run out of memory where one alone runs.

docs.text: candidate link opened why not DOGraspNet's offset crop (code) huamo555/DOGraspNet LICENSE graspnet-baseline non-commercial licence. docs.title: Grasp heads and losses: what is predicted per seed and how it is penalised
docs.text:
Words such as seed, contract, preset, adapter, label set and point painting are explained in the slot index.

Which of these options fit a method

Every method has a page that lists the options of each of its slots with what was measured for each (the verdict, the levels composes, runs, learns and predicts, the class, the grasps, the reason of a refusal): GSNet (head bundle, assigner, losses); EconomicGrasp (head bundle, assigner, losses); FineGrasp (head bundle, assigner, losses); GraspNet-baseline (head bundle, assigner, losses); Scale-Balanced-Grasp (head bundle, assigner, losses). In a terminal: grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list head.

Class: one run, seed 0, 20 iterations, 8 frames of one scene; a class counts verdicts, not accuracy. Where this page names a class or a measured verdict, it is one of the measured classes.

docs.title: 1. The task of the slot
docs.text:
A seed-based detector (GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp, GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp) picks seed points, chooses an approach direction per seed, crops the scene around the seed along that direction, and then has to say which grasp to execute there: the in-plane rotation, how deep the fingers go, how wide they open, and how good the grasp is. That last step is the head bundle (model.head). It is the last stage of the network: grouper → head → GraspGroup.

A head bundle is four parts that cannot be mixed across bundles, because they share one grasp parameterisation: the network head, the target encoder (labels → what the head is trained on), the loss, and the decoder (outputs → grasps). So the bundle is swapped as a whole. Inside a bundle, and inside the proposal and view stages before it, every loss term is a small config node of its own ({type: SmoothL1, weight: 10.0}); those are swapped one by one. This page covers both: head bundles, and the loss primitives that go into the loss terms of any stage.

No AP is claimed for any option of this page. What was checked is that each one builds, trains a few iterations on real frames with finite losses and predicts (the measured records), and a unit test of its contract.

docs.title: The head bundle
docs.text:
class HeadBundle(nn.Module):
    def forward(self, crops: GroupFeatures) -> Predictions: ...        # raw outputs, with gradients
    def encode(self, matched: MatchedLabels, ...) -> Targets: ...      # labels -> targets
    def loss(self, predictions, targets, ...) -> dict[str, Tensor]:    # named, weighted terms
    def decode(self, raw, seeds, approach, gripper) -> GraspGroup: ... # one grasp per seed
in: crop features from the grouper, one row per valid seed. Their named axes are the grouper's out_axes: ('seed', 'channel') (CylinderGroup, CylinderInteractionGroup, MultiScaleGroup) or ('seed', 'depth', 'channel') (DepthCylinderGroup, one crop per depth bin). in: matched labels from the assigner, the labels of the scene point nearest to every seed, already reduced to the chosen view: dense (a friction and a width per in-plane angle and depth bin) or compact (one best grasp per seed). out, training a dictionary of named loss terms, each already multiplied by its weight; the trainer sums them and logs each as loss/<name>. out, prediction a GraspGroup with one grasp per seed: translation (the seed, metres, camera frame), rotation (approach from the view stage, in-plane angle from the head), depth, width (metres), score.

Contract attributes of a head bundle, and what the config checker does with them:

attribute meaning rule in_axes axes of the crop features it expects must equal the grouper's out_axes label_format dense or compact must equal the assigner's label_format (and the dataset must serve that label set) score_kind meaning of the decoded score scores of different kinds are not comparable; shown in the catalogue applies_seed_weights whether its loss honours a weight per seed from the assigner an assigner that returns weights needs a head that applies them loss_terms loss option → kind of term (below) every loss node is checked against it

docs.title: A loss primitive
docs.text:
class Loss(nn.Module):
    def forward(self, prediction, target, mask=None, weights=None) -> Tensor  # weight x mean over the supervised elements

A stage declares the kind of every loss option it has, a primitive the kinds it accepts. There are four kinds:

kind what the stage hands to the loss examples class (N, C) logits against (N,) class indices objectness of points or seeds; angle, depth and quality classes unit prediction and target of equal shape, the target a quality in [0, 1] graspness, view scores of TemplateViewStage, the score grid of SWADHead value prediction and target of equal shape, the target unbounded widths, tolerances, the log-friction scores of the GraspNet-baseline family (up to ln 10) bins (N, C) logits over bins against (N,) fractional bin positions the width of DecoupledGridHead with width: bins

Which term of which stage is which kind (the stages of the five shipped methods):

stage option (write it as <slot>.<option>) kind loss in the shipped configs GraspnessFPS (GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp) proposal.objectness_loss class CrossEntropy proposal.graspness_loss unit SmoothL1 TemplateViewStage (GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp) view.loss unit SmoothL1 LatticeViewStage, IcosphereViewStage, HealpixViewStage (view slot) view.loss unit with target: score, class with target: best_view SmoothL1 / CrossEntropy ObjectnessViewStage (GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp) view.objectness_loss class CrossEntropy view.view_loss value MSE SWADHead (GSNet) head.score_loss unit SmoothL1 head.width_loss value SmoothL1 EconomicHead (EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp) head.angle_loss, head.depth_loss, head.score_loss class CrossEntropy head.width_loss value SmoothL1 OperationHead (GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp) head.angle_loss class CrossEntropy head.score_loss, head.width_loss, head.tolerance_loss value SmoothL1 DecoupledGridHead (new) head.score_loss unit SmoothL1 head.angle_loss class CrossEntropy head.depth_loss class or value (option depth) CrossEntropy / SmoothL1 head.width_loss value, class or bins (option width) SmoothL1 / CrossEntropy / DistributionFocal

The config checker refuses a loss in a term of another kind and names the losses that fit. Two further attributes of a primitive matter:

  • prediction: value or logit. A loss that trains the output of a unit term as a logit (QualityFocal, Varifocal, GHMC, FocalLoss, BinaryCrossEntropy) changes what the raw output means. The stages read it through the sigmoid where they consume it: GraspnessFPS compares the graspness with its threshold, SWADHead decodes its score.
  • applies_weights: false for a loss that scores the supervised set as a whole (DiceLoss, LovaszSoftmaxLoss). It is refused in a term that receives a weight per seed from the assigner (Scale-Balanced-Grasp).

grasppanda components <Loss> prints both and the accepted kinds.

docs.title: Losses
docs.text:
"Name" is the preset to write after --set <slot>.<option>=; "component" is the type: of a config node. "Probed" is what the measured records hold (measured combinations, group loss): the terms the loss was put into on real frames, all with the verdict runs unless stated. Every loss goes into every term of a kind it accepts, in any stage of any seed-based method (a contract, not a measured class); that it does is a unit test on tiny models of four methods (tests/unit/test_losses_zoo.py). The measured grid also has a cell for every loss in one term of each kind it fits, under every seed-based method with such a term (the last term of that kind in the pipeline, the one nearest the grasp); the measured page lists those terms and which of the cells are not probed yet. Nothing here has weights.
