docs.title: 4.1 A new encoder under a method
docs.text:
grasppanda compose --list backbone                 # the presets, one line each
grasppanda compose --show backbone=minkunet18a     # one preset with its notes
grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
    --set backbone=minkunet18a -o gsnet_minkunet18a.yaml
grasppanda probe gsnet_minkunet18a.yaml            # a few iterations on real frames
grasppanda train gsnet_minkunet18a.yaml

The other four methods: economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e, finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e, graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e, scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e. Under the last two compose wraps the encoder in FurthestPointSubsample by itself:

$ grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e \
      --set backbone=minkunet18a-openscene -o gnb_openscene.yaml

slot      component                           from
────────  ──────────────────────────────────  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
backbone  MinkUNet in FurthestPointSubsample  preset `minkunet18a-openscene`, in the adapter FurthestPointSubsample
proposal  SubsampledSeeds                     base config
view      ObjectnessViewStage                 base config
assigner  NearestLabelAssigner                base config
grouper   DepthCylinderGroup                  base config
head      OperationHead                       base config

what compose did
  • backbone: preset `minkunet18a-openscene` (MinkUNet). MinkUNet18A started from the OpenScene
    weights (distilled from CLIP features, ScanNet).
  • out_channels: 256, the output width of the encoder it replaces (PointNet2), so that the other
    stages keep the width they have in the base model and the encoder is the only stage that
    differs.
  • wrapped MinkUNet in the adapter FurthestPointSubsample (preset `furthest-point-subsample`):
    SubsampledSeeds requires 'subsampled' scene features, but MinkUNet returns 'dense' ones (one
    feature per scene point). An adapter changes the model; its notes below say how.
  ...
config check
  ✓ valid  (hash 1943062dfa2b)

The same as a YAML fragment, for a config written by hand (any member of the family):

model:
  backbone:
    type: MinkUNet
    in_channels: 3            # what the method feeds: 3 ones, or 6 under FineGrasp
    out_channels: 512         # free 1x1 projection; null returns the decoder width (96)
    voxel_size: 0.005         # the encoder's unit of length, in metres
    layers: [2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2]
    planes: [32, 64, 128, 256, 128, 128, 96, 96]
    stem_kernel: 5            # 5 in MinkUNet; 3 in the Res16UNet34C checkpoints

Settings that matter, for all sparse encoders:

  • voxel_size / grid_size: 0.005 m keeps the grid of the reference methods, with about one point per voxel. Weights from room-scale data were trained at 0.02 to 0.025 m; choosing that grid matches the weights and leaves a table-top frame with far fewer voxels (a surface has roughly a sixteenth of them at four times the edge). There is no published answer for grasping; it is the first thing to sweep (--opts model.backbone.voxel_size=0.01).
  • out_channels: the width the later stages are built with. compose keeps the width of the encoder it replaces. For the transformer encoders it is fixed by the architecture.
  • depth against the recipe: the reference recipes (Adam, 1e-3, no warm-up) were tuned for a 14-layer network. Deeper encoders and pretrained ones usually want a lower rate and a warm-up; none of this was tuned here.

docs.title: 4.2 Starting from released weights
docs.text:
1. Pick a row of table 3.2 and fetch the file into $GRASPPANDA_CACHE/weights_components/. You do not need to look up the link: build the model once and the error prints the command.

    SpUNet: the released weights `gaussiancross-scannet-lin` (GaussianCross (Yao et al., ACM MM 2025);
MIT; 157 MB) are not on this machine. Fetch them with
  mkdir -p $GRASPPANDA_CACHE/weights_components && curl -L -o $GRASPPANDA_CACHE/weights_components/spunet_gaussiancross_scannet_lin.pth https://huggingface.co/RayYoh/GaussianCross/resolve/3cbceee8b88113780cec6a734fea8b14e2baae4f/scannet/semseg-spunet-base-lin/model/model_best.pth
or set `pretrained: null` to build the encoder without them (for example to load a grasp
checkpoint that already holds the encoder).

  2. Compose with the preset of that release, or add two lines to any config of the class:

    model:
  backbone:
    type: SpUNet
    in_channels: 3
    out_channels: 512
    grid_size: 0.005
    pretrained: gaussiancross-scannet-lin   # a name of table 3.2, or a file path
    pretrained_mismatch: skip               # see below

  3. Read the load report in the log. It names every tensor that did not come from the file. These are the reports of three presets, as printed:

    SpUNet: pretrained weights from $GRASPPANDA_CACHE/weights_components/spunet_gaussiancross_scannet_lin.pth (prefix `module.backbone.`): 353 tensors loaded; 2 absent from the file (final.weight, final.bias); 1 of another shape (conv_input.0.weight (32, 5, 5, 5, 6) in the file, (32, 5, 5, 5, 3) here); 2 tensors outside the encoder ignored
MinkUNet: pretrained weights from $GRASPPANDA_CACHE/weights_components/minkunet18a_openscene_scannet_openseg.pth.tar (prefix `net3d.`): 288 tensors loaded; 1 absent from the file (final.bias); 1 of another shape (final.weight (768, 96) in the file, (512, 96) here)
PTv3: pretrained weights from $GRASPPANDA_CACHE/weights_components/ptv3_ppt_s3dis.pth (prefix `module.backbone.`): 507 tensors loaded; 1 of another shape (embedding.stem.conv.weight (32, 5, 5, 5, 6) in the file, (32, 5, 5, 5, 3) here); 5 tensors outside the encoder ignored

How the option behaves:

  • What is loaded. The encoder alone. The loader finds the prefix under which the file keeps it (module.backbone., net3d., model.backbone., none), ignores heads and optimiser state, and re-lays kernels where the original library stores them differently (Pointcept 1×1 kernels for SpUNet, MinkowskiEngine kernels for MinkUNet).
  • pretrained_mismatch: error (the default) refuses when a tensor of the encoder is absent from the file or has another shape there. Use it with the options of table 3.2 to be sure that everything came from the file.
  • pretrained_mismatch: skip keeps the initialisation of exactly those tensors and lists them. A grasp model needs it almost always, because of two layers: the stem (the releases read 6 or 9 real channels, colour and normal; the grasp methods feed 3 ones) and the final projection when out_channels differs. Everything between them is loaded.
  • No pickled code runs. Training checkpoints of research code pickle schedulers and numpy scalars; the reader maps every such name to an inert object and reads only tensors.
  • Prompt-driven normalisation (ptv3-ppt): the checkpoint holds three sets of normalisation layers, one per training dataset. pretrained_condition: 0 | 1 | 2 takes one set; the model itself is a plain PTv3.
  • Encoder-only PTv3 (ptv3-encoder): enc_mode: true builds no decoder and returns the encoder stages concatenated on every voxel (concat_stages). With pretrained: a full checkpoint loads its encoder half; the report lists the 200 decoder tensors as "in the file but not in the model".

Which release for which use, as far as the sources say (none was evaluated for grasping here):

If you want Take Why weights whose input is what the grasp methods feed minkunet18a-openscene trained on three constant ones per point, so stem included everything loads under GSNet, EconomicGrasp, GraspNet-baseline and Scale-Balanced-Grasp language-aligned point features the same, with --opts model.backbone.out_channels=768 model.backbone.final_bias=false the released output layer predicts OpenSeg / CLIP features; the load is then strict pre-training on single partial RGB-D frames minkunet34c-pointcontrast PointContrast trains on pairs of ScanNet frames, the regime of one table-top view permissive licence, self-supervised spunet-gaussiancross MIT on the card supervision from more than one indoor dataset ptv3-ppt trained on ScanNet, S3DIS and Structured3D jointly the smallest download litept-structured3d, ptv3-sonata-small (NC) about 150 MB each

docs.title: 5. Pitfalls met while building this
docs.text:
• A grasp checkpoint still wants the released file. pretrained loads when the encoder is constructed, also when you then load a grasp checkpoint with --weights or resume a run. Keep the file in place, or set pretrained: null for evaluation (the grasp checkpoint holds the whole encoder).
  • The stem is the tensor that does not load, and it is the layer that reads the input. Under FineGrasp compose sets in_channels: 6, so a 6-channel stem does load there, but nothing says that the six channels of that method are the colour and normal, in the scaling, the release was trained on. Loading says nothing about meaning.
  • The default Concerto files are not the paper's Concerto. The model card calls concerto_{tiny,small,base,large}.pth pre-release Utonia models; the paper's model is concerto_base_origin.pth. The card also says the default files accept inputs without colour and normal ("please set them to zeros"), which is closer to what a grasp model has.
  • Licences differ inside one family. PTv3 and LitePT weights are MIT; Sonata and Concerto weights are CC BY-NC 4.0 (the Sonata hub card states no licence, the repository README does). PointContrast, Mask3D and OpenScene publish code under MIT or Apache-2.0 and say nothing about the weights, which were trained on ScanNet.
  • SpUNet is not MinkUNet34C. Same block counts and widths; in Pointcept's network the stride-2 convolution changes the width, in MinkowskiEngine's the first block of the stage does. A checkpoint of one does not fit the other; the loader says "no tensor fits" or lists hundreds of mismatches rather than loading half of it.
  • Two kernel sizes may not share a spconv indice key. A 5³ stem that shared the key of the 3³ blocks of its level built, ran on CPU with a 3³ stem and failed on the GPU with you must provide same algo to layers share same indice key. The stem of MinkUNet has its own key; the unit test runs a 5³ stem.
  • Fixed-width encoders under Scale-Balanced-Grasp used to fail when the model was built (the gated seed residual adds the seed features to 256-channel crop features). The config check compares the widths now and compose puts the projected grouper in place; with --no-adapter the pair is refused with the fix.
  • Old checkpoints in the legacy (non-zip) PyTorch format that pickle foreign objects cannot be read without executing them and are refused (met with the Contrastive Scene Contexts files). Re-save the state dict in the environment that wrote it.
  • Probes on a shared GPU. Several cells first "failed" with CUDA out of memory because other jobs held the card; such records say nothing about the config and were probed again.

docs.title: Scene encoders: transformers, state-space models, pretrained 3-D encoders
docs.text:
Words such as seed, contract, preset, adapter, label set and point painting are explained in the slot index.

Which of these options fit a method

Every method has a page that lists the options of each of its slots with what was measured for each (the verdict, the levels composes, runs, learns and predicts, the class, the grasps, the reason of a refusal): GSNet (scene encoder); EconomicGrasp (scene encoder); FineGrasp (scene encoder); GraspNet-baseline (scene encoder); Scale-Balanced-Grasp (scene encoder). In a terminal: grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list backbone.

Class: one run, seed 0, 20 iterations, 8 frames of one scene; a class counts verdicts, not accuracy. Where this page names a class or a measured verdict, it is one of the measured classes.

Slot model.backbone of the seed-based detectors (GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp, GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp). This page covers the attention-based and sequence-model encoders added from existing code: Point Transformer V1 and V2, Volt, OctFormer, the point-token family (PointViT, PointMamba, Uni3D) and the released weights that fit them. PTv3 (with Sonata, Concerto and Utonia weights), LitePT and the PointNet++ / transformer encoder of Scale-Balanced-Grasp were in the toolbox before; see the backbone zoo.

Nothing on this page is a grasp-detection result. Every option was built, trained for 20 iterations and used for prediction on real GraspNet-1Billion frames under each method (a probe); no AP was measured for any of them, and no released weight was evaluated on grasp data.

docs.title: 1. The task of the slot
docs.text:
The scene encoder turns the point cloud of one depth frame into per-point features. Everything after it reads those features: the proposal stage scores points and picks seeds, the view stage chooses an approach direction per seed, the grouper crops a neighbourhood per seed and the head predicts angle, depth, width and score. The encoder is the only stage that sees the whole scene, so it decides how much context a seed feature carries and most of the model's cost.

Observation.points ──► backbone ──► proposal ──► view ──► grouper ──► head ──► GraspGroup
     PointSet        PointFeatures    SeedSet   ApproachSet GroupFeatures

docs.title: 2. Input and output
docs.text:
class Backbone(nn.Module):                      # grasppanda/models/base.py
    output: ClassVar[Literal["dense", "subsampled"]]
    in_channels: int
    out_channels: int
    def forward(self, points: PointSet, feats: Tensor) -> PointFeatures: ...
points PointSet: coords (N, 3) float32, metres, camera frame, all clouds of the batch concatenated; batch_offsets (B + 1,) marks the clouds. The shipped GraspNet-1Billion pipelines sample 15 000 or 20 000 points per frame after a workspace crop; clouds of a batch may differ in size. feats (N, in_channels) per-point input features, or None when in_channels == 0. The detector feeds constant ones (point_features: ones, in every shipped method except FineGrasp) or what the dataset provides (point_features: observation). returns PointFeatures: feats (M, out_channels) bound to a point set. output = "dense" M == N: one feature per input point, bound to points itself. output = "subsampled" M < N: features on points.subset(index), a child set that remembers which rows of the parent it kept. An equal number of points per cloud.

What the neighbours require, and what the config checker does with it:

  • The proposal stage declares requires. GSNet, EconomicGrasp and FineGrasp score every scene point (GraspnessFPS: dense); GraspNet-baseline and Scale-Balanced-Grasp take the encoder's subsample as their seeds (SubsampledSeeds: subsampled, and the number of kept points must be proposal.num_seeds, 1024).
  • A mismatch is refused before anything is built, and the message names the adapter: FeaturePropagation (three-neighbour interpolation back to every point) makes a subsampled encoder dense; FurthestPointSubsample makes a dense encoder subsampled. grasppanda compose inserts the adapter itself and says so.
  • out_channels is the in_channels of proposal, view stage and grouper, injected by the detector. Scale-Balanced-Grasp adds seed features to crop features, so there the encoder must be exactly as wide as the crop features (256). Every encoder of this page has an out_channels option, which compose sets to the width of the encoder it replaces (512 under the sparse U-Net methods, 256 under the PointNet++ methods).
  • Features must not mix clouds of a batch. All encoders here keep that in evaluation mode, with two documented exceptions: OctFormer (attention groups are cut from the nodes of the whole batch, as upstream) and, within float noise of its CUDA kernel, PointMamba.

docs.title: 4. How to use each option
docs.text:
One command composes a config, a second one probes it:

$ grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --set backbone=volt -o gsnet_volt.yaml
$ grasppanda probe gsnet_volt.yaml

compose prints what it changed. Two real examples, the same encoder under a method that wants subsampled features and under one that wants dense ones:

$ grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e --set backbone=point-vit -o baseline_point-vit.yaml

slot      component             from
────────  ────────────────────  ──────────────────
backbone  PointViT              preset `point-vit`
proposal  SubsampledSeeds       base config
...
what compose did
  • backbone: preset `point-vit` (PointViT). Plain transformer over 1024 point-patch tokens (the
    Point-BERT / Point-MAE encoder).
  • out_channels: 256, the output width of the encoder it replaces (PointNet2), so that the other
    stages keep the width they have in the base model and the encoder is the only stage that
    differs.
config check
  ✓ valid  (hash 5d1fec9f95b3)

$ grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --set backbone=point-vit -o gsnet_point-vit.yaml

slot      component                       from
────────  ──────────────────────────────  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
backbone  PointViT in FeaturePropagation  preset `point-vit`, in the adapter FeaturePropagation
...
  • wrapped PointViT in the adapter FeaturePropagation (preset `feature-propagation`): GraspnessFPS
    requires 'dense' scene features, but PointViT returns 'subsampled' ones (features on a
    sub-sampled point set). An adapter changes the model; its notes below say how.

To change an option of the preset, add --opts model.backbone.<option>=<value> to compose, or write the fragment into your own config. The fragments below are the presets; the comments say which settings matter.

docs.title: Point Transformer V1
docs.text:
model:
  backbone:
    type: PointTransformerV1
    in_channels: 3                 # constant ones
    out_channels: 512              # optional projection; omit for the 32-channel decoder
    # blocks: [1, 2, 3, 5, 2]      # Seg50, the model of the paper (default: Seg26)

No metric setting: sub-sampling is by ratio (÷4 per stage), neighbourhoods are 8 or 16 nearest points. A cloud needs at least 256 points (the product of the strides).

docs.title: Point Transformer V2
docs.text:
model:
  backbone:
    type: PointTransformerV2
    in_channels: 3
    out_channels: 512
    grid_sizes: [0.015, 0.0375, 0.09375, 0.234375]   # metres; the ScanNet values ÷ 4

grid_sizes is the setting that matters: the cell edge of the four poolings, in metres. The class defaults (0.06 … 0.94 m) are for rooms. pe_multiplier: true gives the paper's PT-v2m1 attention; the default is PT-v2m2, which the Pointcept README recommends.

docs.title: Volt
docs.text:
model:
  backbone:
    type: Volt
    in_channels: 3
    out_channels: 512
    up_mlp_dim: 128
    grid_size: 0.005               # voxel edge, metres
    kernel_size: 5                 # voxels per token and axis: tokens of 2.5 cm
    embed_dim: 384                 # Volt-S; 768 with num_heads: 12 is Volt-B
    num_heads: 6                   # embed_dim / num_heads must be 64 (rope_split)
    qk_norm: true

grid_size × kernel_size is the edge of a token. Smaller tokens resolve finer geometry and cost quadratically more attention. The authors state that Volt overfits without their training recipe (strong augmentation, distillation from a sparse U-Net, EMA); that recipe is not part of this toolbox.

docs.title: OctFormer
docs.text:
$ pip install -e ".[ocnn]"

model:
  backbone:
    type: OctFormer
    in_channels: 3
    out_channels: 512
    voxel_size: 0.005              # edge of an octree leaf, metres
    # octree_depth: 11             # a frame must fit a cube of voxel_size * 2**depth
    # patch_size: 26               # octree nodes per attention group
    # drop_path: 0.5               # the ScanNet recipe; lower it for short schedules

docs.title: PointViT, PointMamba, Uni3D (point-patch tokens)
docs.text:
$ pip install -e ".[timm]"         # Uni3D
$ pip install -e ".[mamba-ssm]"    # PointMamba; or a wheel from the mamba releases page

model:
  backbone:
    type: PointViT                 # or PointMamba, or Uni3D
    in_channels: 0                 # coordinates only (Uni3D: 3, colour or constant ones)
    num_group: 1024                # tokens per cloud = points with features = seeds
    group_size: 32                 # nearest points per token (Uni3D: 64)
    coord_scale: 2.0               # metres -> the unit-sphere scale of the object models
    # PointViT:   embed_dim: 384, depth: 12, num_heads: 6, token_dim: 384 (256: Point-BERT)
    # PointMamba: serialization_grid: 0.02, ssm_cfg: {d_state: 16}
    # Uni3D:      timm_model: eva02_small_patch14_224

num_group must equal proposal.num_seeds under GraspNet-baseline and Scale-Balanced-Grasp (1024 in the shipped configs). PointViT attends globally (quadratic in num_group); PointMamba is linear in it.

docs.title: 5. Released weights
docs.text:
Weights of scene encoders are never downloaded by the toolbox. Download a file, convert it for the config you composed, and start training from it:

$ curl -L -o pretrain.pth https://github.com/Pang-Yatian/Point-MAE/releases/download/main/pretrain.pth
$ python -m tools.convert_encoder_checkpoint pretrain.pth point-mae_for_baseline.pth --config baseline_point-vit.yaml
pretrain.pth: 156 tensors fit PointViT (as `backbone.*`), 53 dropped (decoders, tokens, heads)
  left at their initial values: proj.weight, proj.bias
wrote point-mae_for_baseline.pth
$ grasppanda train baseline_point-vit.yaml --opts runtime.load_from=point-mae_for_baseline.pth runtime.allow_weight_mismatch=true

A probe started from that file ran (the trainer lists the keys the file does not hold):

$ grasppanda probe baseline_point-vit.yaml --opts runtime.load_from=point-mae_for_baseline.pth runtime.allow_weight_mismatch=true
    loss                        3.411 → 1.342
  predicted   2 frame(s) · 493, 482 grasps
✓ runs: trained 20 iterations on 8 frames of the dataset and predicted on 2 frame(s), with finite losses and real seeds in every iteration.

Under a method where compose wrapped the encoder in an adapter the tool writes the keys as backbone.backbone.*; it reads that from the config. With sizes that do not match, nothing is written:

$ python -m tools.convert_encoder_checkpoint maskpoint_pretrain_shapenet.pth out.pth --config baseline_point-vit.yaml
maskpoint_pretrain_shapenet.pth: 154 tensors fit PointViT (as `backbone.*`), 26 dropped (decoders, tokens, heads)
  left at their initial values: proj.weight, proj.bias
  shape differs: module.transformer_q.encoder.second_conv.3.weight: file (256, 512, 1), model (384, 512, 1)
  shape differs: module.transformer_q.encoder.second_conv.3.bias: file (256,), model (384,)
  not in the file: encoder.second_conv.3.weight
  not in the file: encoder.second_conv.3.bias
Nothing was written: set the encoder sizes of the config to those of the file (for example `token_dim: 256` for Point-BERT and MaskPoint files), or name what may stay new with --fresh.

Files that were downloaded and loaded in this work (every tensor of the encoder found with its shape, then a forward pass; tests/integration/test_encoder_checkpoints.py repeats it when the files lie under $GRASPPANDA_WEIGHTS/components/):

File (size) Fits Encoder options Trained on Licence SHA-256 (first 16) Point-MAE pretrain.pth (348 MB) PointViT defaults ShapeNet objects, masked autoencoding repository MIT; no separate statement for the file 27ded932bb0a2625 MaskPoint pretrain_shapenet.pth (286 MB) PointViT token_dim: 256 (the Point-BERT layout) ShapeNet objects, masked discrimination (ECCV 2022) repository BSD-3-Clause; no separate statement for the file 8173353d4117669c PointMamba pretrain.pth (64 MB) PointMamba defaults ShapeNet objects repository Apache-2.0; no separate statement for the file 3d1a89683d8b135d Uni3D uni3d-ti/model.pt (13 MB) Uni3D timm_model: eva02_tiny_patch14_224 object collections with colour, aligned with CLIP (see the Uni3D README) code MIT; the model card states no licence 6ff7e821e6997cb8 Uni3D uni3d-s/model.pt (46 MB) Uni3D timm_model: eva02_small_patch14_224 (the preset) same same 9a6342fda2245f00 Volt-S joint_training_small/scannet/model/model_last.pth (381 MB) Volt embed_dim: 384, num_heads: 6, qk_norm: true, up_mlp_dim: 128, in_channels: 6, grid_size: 0.02 ScanNet, ScanNet200, ScanNet++, ARKitScenes jointly, with distillation (its config) MIT (model card) 2ce43d64b17999fa

What these weights are and are not:

  • All but Volt were trained on single objects scaled to the unit sphere, 1024 to 10 000 points, 64 to 512 tokens. On a metric scene with 1024 tokens of 2 cm they are an initialisation of the transformer, not a feature extractor.
  • Volt-S was trained on rooms with colour and normal as input on a 2 cm grid. With the preset (three constant channels, 5 mm grid) the tokeniser has another shape; give --fresh tokenizer.proj to the tool to keep the transformer and the decoder and start the tokeniser anew. This was run:

$ python -m tools.convert_encoder_checkpoint volt-small-scannet.pth volt-s_for_gsnet.pth --config gsnet_volt.yaml --fresh tokenizer.proj
volt-small-scannet.pth: 211 tensors fit Volt (as `backbone.*`), 16 dropped (decoders, tokens, heads)
  left at their initial values: tokenizer.proj.weight, head.0.weight, head.1.weight, head.1.bias, head.1.running_mean, head.1.running_var, head.1.num_batches_tracked
wrote volt-s_for_gsnet.pth
* The larger Uni3D files (uni3d-b, -l, -g: 178 MB to 2 GB) and the other Volt experiments have the same layout by their configs; they were not downloaded.

docs.title: 6. Pitfalls met
docs.text:
• mamba-ssm on PyPI is a source build. Prebuilt wheels per torch / CUDA / Python version are on the releases page; mamba_ssm-2.3.2.post1+cu11torch2.7cxx11abiTRUE-cp312 was used here (installed with --no-deps).
  • import mamba_ssm compiles a Triton helper and fails with /usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lcuda when the machine has libcuda.so.1 but no libcuda.so. Point Triton at a directory that holds a link of that name: mkdir libcuda && ln -s /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 libcuda/libcuda.so && export TRITON_LIBCUDA_PATH=$PWD/libcuda.
  • PointMamba has no CPU path (the selective scan is a CUDA kernel). On the CPU it raises PointMamba runs on CUDA only ...; its unit tests need a GPU.
  • ocnn 2.3.3 runs its 3×3×3 convolutions on Triton kernels by default on CUDA; with the Triton 3.3.1 of this environment they did not compile (triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError). OctFormer therefore sets ocnn's pure-PyTorch path (conv_method: block_gemm); conv_method: triton asks for the kernels. import ocnn itself needs triton to be importable.
  • OctFormer's features depend on the batch: attention groups are fixed counts of z-ordered nodes of the whole batch, so where a group starts inside a frame depends on the frames before it. This is the reference behaviour.
  • Object checkpoints use other sizes than the first config you try. MaskPoint's ShapeNet file has the Point-BERT layout (token_dim: 256); MaskPoint's ScanNet file (pretrain_scannet_medium_enc12x.pth) is a 3DETR encoder and does not fit PointViT (2 of 156 tensors matched).
  • Width under Scale-Balanced-Grasp. An encoder that returns 32 channels is refused at build time by the gated seed residual of DepthCylinderGroup (it met PointTransformerV1 before that class had out_channels). Keep out_channels at the value compose sets.
  • Memory at scene size (one forward and backward pass, 35 000 points in two clouds, random weights, RTX A6000 shared with other jobs; a rough guide, not a benchmark): PointTransformerV1 1.4 GiB, PointTransformerV2 6.2 GiB, Volt (Volt-S, 2.5 cm tokens of a 0.6 × 0.6 m slab) 2.1 GiB, OctFormer 1.0 GiB (leaves of 1 cm), PointViT 2.7 GiB, PointMamba 2.6 GiB.

docs.title: 7. Not wrapped
docs.text: Candidate Opened Why not Swin3D (Microsoft) microsoft/Swin3D @ 57d5137, MIT Built on MinkowskiEngine (requirements.txt, Swin3D/models/Swin3D.py) plus its own CUDA package; neither is a dependency of this toolbox, and MinkowskiEngine has no build for this stack. Superpoint Transformer / EZ-SP drprojects/superpoint_transformer @ 6bcee31, MIT Needs a superpoint partition computed outside the network (pgeof, pycut-pursuit, FRNN, built by its install.sh); the model consumes that hierarchy, not a PointSet. It does not fit forward(points, feats) without a preprocessing stage. Mamba3D (ACM MM 2024) xhanxu/Mamba3D @ b519a9c No licence file in the repository. Point Cloud Mamba SkyworkAI/PointCloudMamba @ 57fdb29 No licence file in the repository. PointGPT (NeurIPS 2023) CGuangyan-BIT/PointGPT @ 9ba3d40, MIT Same tokeniser, but its blocks are nn.MultiheadAttention in a GPT extractor (models/GPT.py): the checkpoints do not fit PointViT without a second block type. Not done. ReCon, ACT (ICLR 2023), PCP-MAE (NeurIPS 2024 Spotlight), Point-JEPA, Point-BERT's own file qizekun/ReCon @ 51a8be0, RunpeiDong/ACT @ d580115, aHapBean/PCP-MAE @ 33b896d, Ayumu-J-S/Point-JEPA @ c36b51c, Julie-tang00/Point-BERT @ ce5a6e1 Checkpoints are behind Google Drive or Tsinghua Cloud links and were not downloaded, so nothing is claimed. The converter strips the MAE_encoder. / transformer_q. prefixes these families use; whether every tensor fits PointViT is untested (ReCon adds image and text tokens). docs.title: Slot view: approach direction and orientation
docs.text:
Words such as seed, contract, preset, adapter, label set and point painting are explained in the slot index.

Which of these options fit a method

Every method has a page that lists the options of each of its slots with what was measured for each (the verdict, the levels composes, runs, learns and predicts, the class, the grasps, the reason of a refusal): GSNet (view); EconomicGrasp (view); FineGrasp (view); GraspNet-baseline (view); Scale-Balanced-Grasp (view). In a terminal: grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list view.

Class: one run, seed 0, 20 iterations, 8 frames of one scene; a class counts verdicts, not accuracy. Where this page names a class or a measured verdict, it is one of the measured classes.

Nothing on this page carries an AP. "Runs" means: the combination passes the contract check, builds, trains 20 iterations on real GraspNet-1Billion frames with finite losses and predicts. How good a choice is takes a full training and an evaluation.

docs.title: 1. What the slot does
docs.text:
model.view is the third stage of the seed-based detectors (GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp, GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp):

backbone → proposal → VIEW → (assigner, training only) → grouper → head bundle

A 6-DoF grasp orientation has three degrees of freedom. The view stage fixes the first two, the approach direction (the unit vector from the gripper towards the object). The head bundle then predicts the third one, the in-plane rotation about that direction, together with depth and width, from a crop of the scene that the grouper cuts in the frame the view stage chose. So the view stage decides what the head gets to look at.

docs.title: Input and output
docs.text:
Called as approach, seeds = view(seeds) Receives SeedSet: M seeds of the whole batch (frames concatenated), seeds.points.coords (M, 3) in metres in the camera frame, seeds.feats (M, C); C is injected by the detector (in_channels) Returns ApproachSet with one row per seed, and the SeedSet (a stage may add a residual to feats, add a score to scores, or mark seeds invalid) ApproachSet.direction (M, 3) unit vectors, camera frame. Read by the decoder of every head bundle: the grasp rotation is approach_to_rotation(direction, in-plane angle) ApproachSet.rotation (M, 3, 3), column 0 = the direction, column 1 horizontal (approach_to_rotation). Read by the grouper at inference as the crop frame. Required ApproachSet.view_index (M,) index into view.template, the lattice the label files are indexed by (300 Fibonacci views). Read by the assigner in training, which looks up the labels of that view and returns the training crop frame (object pose × template frame of that view). Required by both assigners ApproachSet.logits whatever the stage needs for its own loss Owns view.loss(approach, matched) -> {"loss/…": scalar, "metric/…": scalar} and its targets, computed from the labels the assigner matched Must have the attribute template (a ViewTemplate with as many views as the label set): the detector hands it to the assigner Declares label_formats (kinds of matched labels it can read: dense grids view_friction (M, V, A, D), compact scores view_graspness (M, V)), needs_matched (optional label fields it cannot do without), seed_scores (scores it adds to the seeds), applies_seed_weights (whether its loss honours the per-seed weight of a scale-balanced assigner)

Three facts about the neighbours shape every option here:

  1. The labels know 300 directions. GraspNet-1Billion and GraspClutter6D grasp labels are indexed by a 300-view Fibonacci lattice, and the assigners address labels by view_index into it. A stage may predict on another lattice, or no lattice at all, but it must snap its choice to one of those 300 for the label lookup, and its targets can never be finer than they are.
  2. Train and inference crops differ by the snap. In training the crop frame is the label frame of the snapped view; at inference it is the frame of the direction the stage returned. For a stage whose directions are the 300 label views the two are the same up to the re-indexing of the labels under the object pose; for every other stage they differ by up to the lattice spacing (table in section 5).
  3. The head still owns the in-plane angle. All registered head bundles decode approach_to_rotation(direction, angle bin). A stage that regresses a full rotation therefore contributes its first column; the rest is an auxiliary output (RegressedApproach.frame) that is supervised and logged. A head bundle that takes the full frame from the view stage does not exist yet (section 7).

docs.title: 2. Which option when
docs.text:
You want Take Why the reference behaviour of GSNet / EconomicGrasp / FineGrasp template-view a score per label view, training view sampled from the scores the reference behaviour of GraspNet-baseline / Scale-Balanced-Grasp objectness-view, objectness-view-graspable also predicts objectness, which their decoders read the same view scoring, but with seed weights or as a base for the options below lattice-view computes what template-view computes (tested with shared weights), and applies the weights of ScaleBalancedAssigner a smaller output layer / coarser choice lattice-fibonacci-120, icosphere-162, healpix-192 fewer classes; each view is supervised by its nearest label view only approaches away from the camera lattice-hemisphere-60 the 60-of-120 template of RGB Matters a classification problem instead of 300 regressions lattice-best-view softmax cross-entropy on the most graspable view ... where near misses are cheap lattice-angular-cost adds the angular class loss of RGB Matters a direction between lattice points at inference lattice-soft-argmax softmax-weighted mean of the top-k view directions training crops closer to what inference will choose lattice-topk samples the training view among the 10 best views instead of all 300 no lattice in the output at all direction-regression 3 numbers per seed, cosine loss ... with a confidence of the direction direction-vmf direction + concentration, von Mises-Fisher likelihood a full grasp frame from two vectors two-vector, two-vector-baseline Gram-Schmidt in the order of the 6-D representation, or of Contact-GraspNet a full rotation in a representation of your choice rotation-6d, rotation-9d, rotation-quaternion (or representation: rotvec) the mappings of RoMa

All options that are not marked "reference" make no demand of their own: they read dense or compact labels, add no seed score, need no optional label field and apply seed weights, so the contract rules accept them behind every proposal and assigner and in front of every grouper and head bundle. With one stage replaced they are most in the words of the measured page: they work under four of the five seed-based methods. The refusal is under Scale-Balanced-Grasp, and it is the head's: its decoder multiplies by the objectness of a seed, which only ObjectnessViewStage predicts (section 4, last example).

There are no pretrained weights for any of the new stages: all start from random initialisation. Released checkpoints of the six ported methods contain TemplateViewStage or ObjectnessViewStage; loading one into a model with another view stage leaves the view stage (and nothing else) untrained.

What each parameterisation demands:

Stage From the labels From the assigner From the head bundle lattice stages (Lattice, Icosphere, Healpix) per seed, the graspness of all 300 label views: dense view_friction (M, 300, A, D) or compact view_graspness (M, 300) encoded with the same max_friction label lookup at view_index; weight is applied when returned nothing DirectionViewStage the same; reduced to the single most graspable view the same nothing TwoVectorViewStage, RomaRotationViewStage the same, plus for the frame target the grid of the snapped view (dense friction (M, A, D)) or its labelled angle bin (compact angle (M,)) additionally crop_rotation, the label frame of the snapped view num_angle equal to the stage's (checked by the contract rules)

docs.title: 4. How to use each option
docs.text:
Every option is one --set:

grasppanda compose --list view                       # the table of presets
grasppanda compose --show view=lattice-soft-argmax   # one preset with its notes
grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --set view=rotation-6d -o my.yaml
grasppanda probe my.yaml                             # 20 iterations on real frames
grasppanda train my.yaml

$ grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --set view=rotation-6d -o my.yaml
slot      component              from
────────  ─────────────────────  ────────────────────
backbone  SparseUNet14           base config
proposal  GraspnessFPS           base config
view      RomaRotationViewStage  preset `rotation-6d`
assigner  NearestLabelAssigner   base config
grouper   CylinderGroup          base config
head      SWADHead               base config
...
contracts
  ✓ backbone · proposal
  ✓ proposal · view
  ✓ view · assigner
  ✓ assigner · head
  ✓ grouper · head
  ✓ view · head
  ✓ proposal · view · head

config check
  ✓ valid  (hash 8347abcb50ef)

The same as a YAML fragment, to paste into a config that inherits a method:

model:
  view:
    type: RomaRotationViewStage
    representation: 6d            # 6d | 9d | quaternion | rotvec
    num_angle: 12                 # must equal the head bundle's

docs.title: Lattice stages
docs.text:
model:
  view:
    type: LatticeViewStage        # or IcosphereViewStage / HealpixViewStage
    num_views: 300                # IcosphereViewStage: subdivisions: 2; HealpixViewStage: nside: 4
    hemisphere: false             # true: only approaches away from the camera
    target: score                 # score | best_view
    selection: argmax             # evaluation: argmax | soft_argmax
    train_selection: multinomial  # training: multinomial | topk | argmax
    top_k: null                   # used by soft_argmax and topk
    temperature: 1.0              # softmax temperature of soft_argmax
    angular_weight: 0.0           # best_view only: weight of the angular class loss
    loss: {type: SmoothL1, weight: 100.0}   # best_view: {type: CrossEntropy, weight: 1.0}
  • Size. LatticeViewStage takes any num_views; IcosphereViewStage has 10 · 4**subdivisions + 2 views (12, 42, 162, 642, 2562); HealpixViewStage has 12 · nside**2 (48, 192, 300, 768 for nside 2, 4, 5, 8). Up to 300 views every view reads its own label column; beyond 300 neighbouring views share one (section 5).
  • target: score is GSNet's: regress the min-max normalised graspness of every view. target: best_view makes it a classification of the most graspable view and logs metric/view_accuracy and metric/view_error_deg; use train_selection: argmax with it, and a CrossEntropy loss.
  • angular_weight adds loss/view_angular: the expected (1 - cos)/2 between the predicted view distribution and the best view. Set the weight of loss to 0 to train with it alone.
  • selection: soft_argmax changes inference only. Choose temperature by the range of the outputs: about 0.05 for regressed scores in [0, 1], 1.0 for logits. Keep top_k small (8) so that two separate good regions are not averaged into the bad region between them.
  • train_selection: topk restricts GSNet's training-time sampling to the top_k best views.

docs.title: Regression stages
docs.text:
model:
  view:
    type: DirectionViewStage
    concentration: false          # true: von Mises-Fisher likelihood, logs metric/view_concentration
    direction_weight: 1.0
---
model:
  view:
    type: TwoVectorViewStage
    keep: approach                # approach (6-D order) | baseline (Contact-GraspNet order)
    direction_weight: 1.0         # loss/view: 1 - cos to the most graspable label view
    frame_weight: 1.0             # loss/view_frame: squared Frobenius distance, half-turn aware
    num_angle: 12
  • loss/view pulls the direction to the most graspable label view; metric/view_error_deg is the mean angle to it.
  • loss/view_frame (two-vector and RoMa stages) compares the regressed frame with the label frame of the snapped view at its best in-plane angle, taking the smaller of the distances to that frame and to its half-turn copy (a parallel-jaw grasp turned by 180° about its approach is the same grasp). metric/view_frame_error_deg is the mean rotation angle.
  • representation of RomaRotationViewStage: 6d and 9d are continuous parameterisations; quaternion and rotvec are not and are there for comparison. rotvec is unit-tested and has no preset and no probe record.
  • residual: true (all new stages) adds the hidden features of the stage to the seed features that the grouper and the head consume, as GSNet's stage does.

docs.title: Under Scale-Balanced-Grasp
docs.text:
$ grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e --set view=lattice-view
  ✗ proposal · view · head: OperationHead as configured reads the seed score 'objectness' when it
    decodes, but neither SubsampledSeeds nor LatticeViewStage predicts it. Use a stage that does
    (proposals: GraspnessFPS, ScoredSeeds; view stages: ObjectnessViewStage) or another decode
    option of the head.

The scale-balanced weights themselves are not the obstacle (the new stages apply them; TemplateViewStage is refused for ignoring them). Take the decode option of the head that does not read objectness:

grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e \
    --set view=lattice-view --set head=operation -o sbg_lattice.yaml

$ grasppanda probe sbg_lattice.yaml --opts data.train.dataset.scale_statistic.source=legacy_import \
      data.train.dataset.scale_statistic.reference_sha256=<SHA-256 of the reference's width histogram>

docs.title: 5. Pitfalls met while building this
docs.text:
• A finer lattice does not give finer labels. Measured with 200 000 random directions (grasppanda.ops lattices, this machine):
Lattice Views Random direction to nearest view, mean / max View to its nearest label view, mean / max Label columns read Fibonacci (the labels) 300 4.5° / 9.0° 0° 300 Fibonacci 120 7.1° / 14.1° 4.6° / 7.7° 120 Fibonacci 1200 2.2° / 4.4° 4.5° / 8.2° 300 icosphere 42 11.9° / 20.8° 4.8° / 7.7° 42 icosphere 162 6.1° / 10.8° 4.5° / 7.7° 162 icosphere 642 3.0° / 5.4° 4.5° / 8.1° 300 HEALPix 48 11.2° / 23.4° 4.5° / 6.7° 48 HEALPix 192 5.6° / 11.5° 4.5° / 7.9° 190 HEALPix 300 4.5° / 9.2° 4.4° / 8.3° 274 HEALPix 768 2.8° / 5.6° 4.5° / 8.4° 300

The third column is the price of a coarse lattice; the fourth is the train/inference crop mismatch of any lattice that is not the label lattice. HEALPix with 192 views already maps two pairs of views onto the same label column. - TemplateViewStage(num_views=N) with N ≠ 300 is not "another lattice size". Its template is also the label lattice, so the assigner refuses the labels at the first loss. Use LatticeViewStage(num_views=N). - Soft-arg-max needs a temperature that fits the outputs. With regressed scores and temperature: 1.0 the weights are nearly uniform and the mean direction is meaningless; with all views voting (top_k: null) opposite views can cancel (the stage then falls back to the best view). - A single best view is a brittle target. best_view, direction-regression and the frame stages reduce the 300 scores of a seed to their arg-max; on a symmetric object two distant views can tie and the target flips between them. target: score and angular_weight do not have this problem to the same degree. - Flip augmentation yields mirrored label frames. crop_rotation of a mirrored object pose is a reflection; the frame loss skips those seeds (their direction loss still counts). - The vMF loss is a log-density and goes negative when the predicted concentration is high. That is not a bug; do not compare its value with the cosine loss. - RomaRotationViewStage imports RoMa in every forward (through the cached require), not as a stored module attribute: a module attribute would make the detector impossible to deep-copy. - healpy is GPL-2.0, so the bridge uses the BSD-licensed healpix package, which ships wheels and needs only NumPy.

docs.title: 6. Not wrapped
docs.text: Candidate Opened Why not Contact-GraspNet code (two-vector head, contact labels, 5-point loss) NVlabs/contact_graspnet its License.pdf is the "NVIDIA Source Code License for Contact-GraspNet"; section 3.3 limits use to non-commercial research and evaluation. The idea of its parameterisation is two-vector-baseline; its contact-point labels and control-point loss need a label asset the toolbox does not have vMF-Contact code YitianShi/vMF-Contact no licence file (the licence request returns 404). The closed form of the likelihood is textbook and is written here; its evidential posterior update is not Generalizing-Grasp code (regressed view with a neighbourhood term, 2θ angle regression) mahaoxiang822/Generalizing-Grasp no licence file. direction-regression is the cosine part of the idea; its soft neighbourhood term is not included S4G (6-D rotation per point, symmetric loss) yzqin/s4g-release no licence file. The same representation and a half-turn-aware loss are in rotation-6d / two-vector DexGraspNet 2.0 (diffusion on seed features) PKU-EPIC/DexGraspNet2 no licence file; a generative head is a head bundle, not a view stage OrbitGrasp, Edge Grasp Network BoceHu/orbitgrasp (MIT), HaojHuang/Edge-Grasp-Network (MIT) detectors of their own (equivariant networks, edge features) with their own simulated labels; they do not fit a seed-feature view stage. Only the licences were checked here healpy, astropy-healpix healpy (GPL-2.0), astropy-healpix (BSD-3-Clause) GPL; and a dependency on astropy for 12·nside² vectors. healpix does the same with NumPy only PyTorch3D rotation conversions facebookresearch/pytorch3d a compiled package for functions RoMa has in pure PyTorch Top-k views per seed at inference (several grasps per location) - ApproachSet is one row per seed and the heads return one grasp per seed; it needs a change of the skeleton, not a view stage A head bundle that takes the regressed in-plane rotation - belongs to the head slot; until it exists the frame of the rotation stages is auxiliary

docs.title: Try a combination
docs.text:
"GSNet with this encoder and that grouper" is four commands:

grasppanda components --slot backbones           # 1. what exists, with its contract
grasppanda compose <config> --set backbone=...   # 2. a checked config for the combination
grasppanda probe <composed config>               # 3. does it really train and predict?
grasppanda train <composed config>               # 4. the experiment itself

Steps 2 and 3 take about a minute together. They tell you whether a combination works: it passes the contracts, builds, trains on real frames with finite losses and predicts. They do not tell you how good it is. No AP is attached to anything on this page; that takes step 4 and an evaluation on a benchmark split.

Which component was found to work under which method is on the generated page Measured combinations; what a swap changes besides the line in the config is in Swapping components. What each option of each slot is, with a command per option, is in Slots.

The same in a browser: the combination explorer answers a selection of method and options from the measured records and prints the commands, and grasppanda explore serves it locally, with every selection checked by the compose of your installation (nothing is trained). Started with weights (grasppanda explore --weights-dir <dir>), its tab Run a method also runs a ported method, or your selection when the weights fit it, on one frame and shows the grasps: Run in the browser.

docs.title: 1. See what exists
docs.text:
grasppanda components is the catalogue (Components): every registered component with the contract the config checker compares. grasppanda compose --list shows the presets:

$ grasppanda compose --list grouper
grouper  --set grouper=<preset or component>
preset                      component                     what it is
──────────────────────────  ────────────────────────────  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ball                        LocalGroup                    LocalGroup with its defaults: a PointNet++ ball among the seeds, shared MLP and max.
box                         LocalGroup                    LocalGroup over a gripper-aligned box with cyclic padding: PointRCNN's RoI point pooling.
...                                                       (25 presets; shortened here)
voxel-set-abstraction       VoxelSetAbstractionGroup      VoxelSetAbstractionGroup with its defaults: PV-RCNN's keypoint feature for every seed.
  components without a preset: CylinderGroup, CylinderInteractionGroup

A component can also be named by its type (`--set grouper=CylinderGroup`): it is then
built with its constructor defaults, which `grasppanda components <type>` lists.
One preset with its notes: grasppanda compose --show <slot>=<preset>.

grasppanda components <name> ends with the presets of that component, and both commands take the slot by either name (grouper, groupers).

docs.title: The options that fit one method
docs.text:
Name a method config before --list and compose lists only the options of that method's slots, each with what was measured for it: the verdict of its probe, the four levels composes, runs, learns and predicts under that method, its class at each level across the methods it applies to, the grasps per frame and the fall of the loss terms; the options that do not fit with the reason, its kind and the lift where the record has them; the options without a record as not probed, with the reason when there is one:

$ grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list view
GSNet · view  (model.view)
measured on gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e (one run, seed 0, 20 iterations, 8 frames of one scene; a class counts verdicts, not accuracy)
...
view  --set view=...   shipped: TemplateViewStage (option template-view)
  fit: 19 (the config check accepts them)
option                   verdict  C R L P  grasps/frame  term fall    class C R L P
───────────────────────  ───────  ───────  ────────────  ───────────  ─────────────
template-view (shipped)  runs     ✓ ✓ ? ?  233, 279      not checked  most most ? ?
direction-regression     runs     ✓ ✓ ? ?  1024, 1024    not checked  most most ? ?
...
  do not fit: 2 (refused by the config check)
    objectness-view: ObjectnessViewStage reads 'on_object' and 'view_width' of the matched labels, ...

Without a slot it lists every slot of the method; --json prints everything, every refusal message whole. The same lists are a page per method (GSNet, HGGD, ...) and the lanes of a method in the explorer, so the three always offer the same options. A config composed from a method config is listed as that method, with a note that the options were measured on the method config. The shipped method configs name the command above each slot. In a wheel the records come with the package; in a checkout they are read from docs/advanced_guides/measured_combinations.json.

A preset is the part of a config a newcomer cannot guess: the settings of one component for table-top depth clouds of GraspNet-1Billion (grid size, radii, widths, sampling rules) and, where its stage reads a label asset, the dataset section that serves it. Its header says what must be re-tuned and why. Every scene encoder has one, because the constructor defaults of most encoders are those of room-scale benchmarks: a bare {type: PTv3} works on a 2 cm grid with six input channels. A stage whose constructor defaults are the reference values of its method needs none.

grasppanda compose --show backbone=ptv3     # the file, with its notes

Presets live in grasppanda/presets/<slot>/<name>.yaml. They are config fragments, not configs, and they are not inherited: two files of one _base_ list may not set the same value, and a preset by definition sets what the method's own model already sets. The values of a preset therefore belong in the child config, which is where compose writes them.

docs.title: 2. Compose
docs.text:
$ grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
      --set backbone=pointnet2 --set grouper=multi-scale -o gsnet_pointnet2_multi-scale.yaml
grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --set backbone=pointnet2 --set grouper=multi-scale

slot      component                        from
────────  ───────────────────────────────  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
backbone  PointNet2 in FeaturePropagation  preset `pointnet2`, in the adapter FeaturePropagation
proposal  GraspnessFPS                     base config
view      TemplateViewStage                base config
assigner  NearestLabelAssigner             base config
grouper   MultiScaleGroup                  preset `multi-scale`
head      SWADHead                         base config

what compose did
  • backbone: preset `pointnet2` (PointNet2). PointNet++ in the GraspNet-baseline layout: features
    on a 1024-point subsample.
  • grouper: preset `multi-scale` (MultiScaleGroup). MultiScaleGroup as FineGrasp uses it: a crop
    among the seeds at four radii, each by an EconomicGrasp crop module of its own, fused per seed
    by attention over the scales.
  • wrapped PointNet2 in the adapter FeaturePropagation (preset `feature-propagation`): GraspnessFPS
    requires 'dense' scene features, but PointNet2 returns 'subsampled' ones (features on a
    sub-sampled point set). An adapter changes the model; its notes below say how.

contracts
  ✓ backbone · proposal
  ✓ backbone · grouper
  ✓ proposal · view
  ✓ view · assigner
  ✓ assigner · head
  ✓ grouper · head
  ✓ view · head
  ✓ proposal · view · head

config check
  ✓ valid  (hash 76e5ab997651)

✓ written gsnet_pointnet2_multi-scale.yaml
  next: grasppanda probe gsnet_pointnet2_multi-scale.yaml

The file is a child config of the method config. Its header repeats the command, what compose did and the re-tuning notes of every preset; its body is what you would have written by hand (shortened here). Outside the shipped config tree the base is named by its absolute path: the file can be moved on this machine, and on another one the command in its header composes it again.

_base_:
  - /…/configs/gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e.yaml

model:
  backbone:
    type: FeaturePropagation      # `subsampled` -> `dense`, written down
    mlp: [256, 256]
    neighbours: 3
    interpolation_power: 1.0
    backbone:
      type: PointNet2             # `subsampled`: features on 1024 points, 256 channels
      in_channels: 0              # coordinates only
      npoints: [2048, 1024, 512, 256]
      radii: [0.04, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3]
      nsamples: [64, 32, 16, 16]
      fps_skip_near_origin: true
      fps_tie_break: pointnet2_cuda
  grouper:
    type: MultiScaleGroup
    radius: 0.07                  # largest crop
    ...

What compose does beyond copying presets, each time saying so:

  • It inserts an encoder adapter when the contract between encoder and proposal refuses the pair and exactly one registered adapter bridges it: FeaturePropagation around a sub-sampling encoder under a proposal that scores every point (above), FurthestPointSubsample around a dense encoder under a proposal that takes the encoder's subsample as its seeds. The adapter gets the seed count of the proposal and the sampling rules of the encoder it replaces. --no-adapter leaves the pair refused.
  • It fits a new encoder to the method. Where the encoder has an out_channels option it is set to the seed width the grouper of the composed model fixes (DepthCylinderGroup with seed_residual: gated adds seed features to its crops) and otherwise to the width of the encoder it replaces, so the other stages keep the width they have in the reference model. Both widths are what the components declare (Backbone.output_channels, Grouper.required_seed_channels); nothing is built.
  • It puts the projected variant of a grouper in place when the encoder has no such option and returns another width than the grouper fixes: DepthCylinderProjectionGroup, the same crop with a linear layer in front of its seed residual (Grouper, section 5). That changes the model, and compose says so; --no-adapter leaves the pair refused.
  • Where the method feeds real point features (point_features: observation, FineGrasp), in_channels is set to their number.
  • It inserts an axis adapter between a grouper and a head bundle whose feature axes differ: DepthEmbedGroup (preset depth-embed) repeats a (seed, channel) crop over the depth bins of the head with a learned embedding of the bin, DepthPoolGroup (preset depth-pool) takes the maximum of a (seed, depth, channel) crop over the bins. --no-adapter leaves the pair refused.
  • It sets the options a stage declares for the other stages: the assigner options that return a field a stage reads (supervise: object_seeds, view_widths: true for ObjectnessViewStage); graspness only for a scoring proposal next to ObjectnessViewStage, which then owns objectness (ScoredSeeds with select_by: graspness_only; GraspnessFPS keeps the options of the reference, so it is replaced by that ScoredSeeds); and the decode option of a head that would multiply in a score no stage predicts (OperationHead with score_decode: score_x_tolerance). Each changes the model and is one sentence of the report; --no-adapter leaves the pair refused.
  • It writes the label set of the head bundle into the recipe. A head of dense label grids on a recipe of compact labels, or the other way round, gets the dataset section of a shipped recipe that serves them (the compact_labels section, or the SampleGraspLabels step) and the assigner of a shipped config that returns them; an assigner you set yourself is kept. --set labels=dense or --set labels=compact asks for it in so many words. Compact labels are an asset to build (grasppanda prepare <dataset> --compact-labels --config <the composed config>); dense grids are read from the label store of grasppanda prepare <dataset> --labels.
  • It adds the dataset section a stage reads, when the preset carries one and the base config has none (scale_statistic for ScaleBalancedAssigner, tolerance for OperationHead, graspness for GraspnessFPS). The asset still has to be built; the preset says how. A component named by its type brings no section: the config check then refuses the config and compose prints the --opts that adds it and the preset that carries it.
  • It puts an option back to its default with --unset key.path (a child config cannot delete what it inherits, so the default of the component is written): --unset data.train.dataset.compact_labels.
  • It replaces, it does not merge. A --set of the same component type as the base config's gets _delete_: true, so no option of the base leaks into what you asked for.
  • It does not overwrite. -o refuses a file that exists unless you pass --force, and never writes onto the base config.

The base is a config that inherits fragments only, like the method configs under configs/<method>/: a config chain is two levels deep, and the composed file is the second. So a composed file cannot be inherited from, but it can be the base of a command: compose reads the request in its header and composes again from its base with the two requests merged.

$ grasppanda compose gsnet_pointnet2_multi-scale.yaml --set head=swad --opts train.epochs=20 -o second.yaml
grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --set backbone=pointnet2 --set grouper=multi-scale --set head=swad --opts train.epochs=20
...
what compose did
  • gsnet_pointnet2_multi-scale.yaml is itself a composed config, and a config chain is limited to 2
    levels: this config is composed from its base, gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e, with its
    request and yours merged (a `--set` of yours replaces the one of the same slot).

A composed file you edited by hand, and a shipped child config such as the cross-dataset …-to-gc6d-d435 ones, are refused as a base with the config to compose from instead.

Further overrides go through --opts; a path below a slot you set addresses that component wherever an adapter put it:

grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --set backbone=ptv3 \
    --opts model.backbone.grid_size=0.01 train.epochs=20 -o gsnet_ptv3_1cm.yaml

No rule about what fits what lives in compose. Every verdict is the contract rules of the config checker, quoted, and a refused combination writes nothing. Each refusal says in brackets why it is one (Swapping, Why a pair is refused): structural (the components cannot work together), not-implemented (a lift not written yet, named in the message), fixed-by-compose (what compose inserts by itself, met with --no-adapter or in a config written by hand), not-a-combination (a component without a required option, two options that disagree) or policy. The --json report lists the same in refusal_kinds, in the order of refusal.

Stages that do not fit each other. A head bundle supervised with compact labels, fed by an assigner of dense ones that you set yourself:

$ grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
      --set assigner=NearestLabelAssigner
...
contracts
  ✓ backbone · proposal
  ✓ backbone · grouper
  ✓ proposal · view
  ✓ view · assigner
  ✗ assigner · head [structural]: NearestLabelAssigner returns 'dense' matched labels, but
    EconomicHead is supervised with 'compact' ones. A head bundle and the assigner that feeds it
    must agree on the label set; the dataset must serve that label set too.
  ✓ grouper · head
  ✓ view · head
  ✓ proposal · view · head

config check
  ✗ data.train.dataset [fixed-by-compose]: NearestLabelAssigner reads `supervision.objects`, which
    this training dataset does not serve. It serves compact labels in place of the dense label grids
    (its `compact_labels` section). A dataset serves one of the two label sets, and its transforms
    differ with it: the dense grids need a `SampleGraspLabels` transform and no `compact_labels`
    section, compact labels the section and no such transform.

✗ refused: nothing was written. The messages above name the conflict and a fix.
  → EconomicHead reads compact labels and NearestLabelAssigner returns dense ones; the request set
    the assigner (`--set assigner=...`). Without it compose gives EconomicHead an assigner and
    training data of compact labels; or keep NearestLabelAssigner with a head bundle that reads
    dense labels (DecoupledGridHead, OperationHead, SWADHead).
  → To make the training data serve the dense labels NearestLabelAssigner reads: `--set
    labels=dense`, which writes `--unset data.train.dataset.compact_labels --opts
    'data.train.dataset.transforms=[{type: RandomSample, num_points: 20000}, {type:
    SampleGraspLabels, point_fraction: 0.25, min_points: 300, collision: zero_scores, grids:
    deferred}, {type: RandomFlip, axis: x, prob: 0.5}, {type: ConstantFeatures, channels: 3}]'` (the
    recipe of gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e).
  → Or compose from a shipped config whose training data serves all of it:
    gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e, gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_gc6d-d435_10e.

The label sets are a genuine difference: a grid of every grasp per point and view cannot be recovered from one grasp. Leave the assigner to compose and the head brings its own labels; swap the head instead and compose rewrites the recipe:

$ grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --set head=swad
...
what compose did
  • head: preset `swad` (SWADHead). SWADHead as GSNet uses it: a score and a width per (angle, depth
    bin) of every seed, regressed; one decoded grasp per seed.
  • labels: dense. SWADHead is supervised with dense labels, and the training data of the base
    config serves compact labels: data.train.dataset now serves dense ones, `compact_labels` unset
    and the SampleGraspLabels step of gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e inserted before
    RandomFlip. The dense grids are read from the label store of `grasppanda prepare <dataset>
    --labels`, which a probe or a run needs (the config check does not look for it). The rest of the
    data recipe is the base config's.
  • assigner: NearestLabelAssigner, the assigner of gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e.
    CompactLabelAssigner returns compact matched labels and SWADHead is supervised with dense ones.

The rest of the data recipe (how many points, the augmentation) stays the base config's.

What compose would insert, refused without it. With --no-adapter, or in a config written by hand, a pair that an adapter or an option joins is refused, and the message names it:

$ grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e \
      --set grouper=ball --no-adapter
...
  ✗ grouper · head [fixed-by-compose]: LocalGroup emits features with axes ('seed', 'channel'), but
    OperationHead expects ('seed', 'depth', 'channel'). An axis is never added or squeezed
    implicitly: wrap the grouper in the axis adapter DepthEmbedGroup (preset `depth-embed`), `{type:
    DepthEmbedGroup, num_depth: <the head's num_depth>, grouper: {...}}`, which `grasppanda compose`
    inserts, or use a grouper and a head bundle that agree. Groupers that emit ('seed', 'depth',
    'channel'): DepthCylinderGroup, DepthCylinderProjectionGroup, DepthEmbedGroup, DepthLocalGroup.
    Head bundles that expect ('seed', 'channel'): DecoupledGridHead, EconomicHead, SWADHead.

A stage set that is accepted but trains differently from what its names promise gets a warning in the report and in the header of the composed file: a stage of a project that does not apply the weight per seed ScaleBalancedAssigner returns trains unweighted.

One more that compose lifts by itself, because it used to surface only when the model was built: an encoder of another width under a grouper that fixes one. The grouper states the width it needs, the encoder the width it returns, and the check compares the two. Compose takes the way out by itself (above); with --no-adapter the pair is refused with both numbers:

$ grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e \
      --set backbone=ptv3 --no-adapter
...
  ✗ backbone · grouper [fixed-by-compose]: DepthCylinderGroup as configured adds the seed features
    to its 256-channel crop features, but PTv3 returns 64-channel features. Use `type:
    DepthCylinderProjectionGroup` for the grouper (the same crop with a linear layer in front of the
    residual; `grasppanda compose` does that), or give the encoder 256 output channels where it has
    that option, or end the grouper's `mlp_channels` on 64, or set `seed_residual: none`.

HGGD is a detector family of its own. It has one component slot, the encoder of its image network (image_encoder, see Image encoders); its other parts are options of the detector, not registered components:

$ grasppanda compose hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e --set image_encoder=resnet34
  • image_encoder: preset `resnet34` (TimmImageEncoder). ResNet-34 from timm with ImageNet-1k
    weights, colour only.
config check
  ✓ valid

$ grasppanda compose hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e --set backbone=ptv3
✗ HGGD has no slot 'backbone'. Its slots: image_encoder. HGGD is a detector family of its own: the
  stages of the seed-based methods (backbone, proposal, view, grouper, head) do not exist in it.
  Its other parts are options of the detector (`grasppanda components HGGD`); change them with
  `--opts model.<part>.<option>=<value>`.

Compose finds slots from the detector class (constructor parameters annotated Cfg[...], or Cfg[...] | None for a slot with a built-in default), so a detector whose parts become registered components is composable without a change here. --opts and probe work for HGGD as for every config.

docs.title: 3. Probe
docs.text:
$ grasppanda probe gsnet_pointnet2_multi-scale.yaml
  config      gsnet_pointnet2_multi-scale.yaml  (hash 76e5ab997651)
  model       GSNet · 4,730,280 parameters
  data        8 frames of the config's dataset · 4 per iteration
  probe       as `grasppanda train` with data.train.dataset.split=sample data.train.num_workers=0 evaluation.interval=0 evaluation.save_best=null train.epochs=10 data.val.dataset.split=sample data.val.dataset.frame_step=4 data.val.num_workers=0
  device      cuda
  trained     20 of 20 iterations · 0.26 s per iteration (median, without data; data 0.34 s), measured on this machine now
  memory      peak 7.6 GiB on the GPU, this process
  losses      first → last · fall from the first active value to the mean of the last quarter
    loss/objectness             0.7068 → 0.6153       fell 9 %
    loss/graspness              0.7984 → 0.3903       fell 51 %
    loss/view                   1.885 → 0.3763        fell 79 %
    loss/score                  0.2622 → 0.0159       fell 93 %
    loss/width                  2.468 → 0.1509        fell 93 %
    loss                        6.12 → 1.549          fell 74 %
  seeds       real: min 1.00, mean 1.00 of the seed slots per iteration
              supervised: 1.00 → 1.00, min 1.00
  predicted   2 frame(s) · 103, 134 grasps
  scores      min / median / max per frame: 0.104 / 0.11 / 0.116; 0.0932 / 0.105 / 0.112
  gradient    reached every one of 9 units of 5 part(s)
  changed     every part
  lr          0.001 at the first step → 0.00063 at the last, ×0.63 at the last step

✓ runs: trained 20 iterations on 8 frames of the dataset and predicted on 2 frame(s), with finite losses and real seeds in every iteration.
  (20 s)

A probe is a miniature of grasppanda train, not a loop of its own: the real trainer, the config's optimizer, schedule, accumulation, clipping and hooks, on the eight frames of the split sample (scene 0 of GraspNet-1Billion, frames 0, 32, …, 224), then prediction on two of them. Nothing is written. The line probe lists the overrides that turn the config into that miniature; with them, grasppanda train runs the same thing.

The schedule of a probe. To fit 20 iterations the probe sets train.epochs to as few epochs as the eight frames need, and the recipe's learning-rate schedule runs over those epochs: GSNet's decay of 0.95 per epoch ends at 0.63 of its rate, EconomicGrasp's cosine at 2.4 %, and FineGrasp's warm-up of 800 iterations keeps the whole probe below 2.5 % of its rate. The trends of two methods are then not comparable. --schedule constant removes the scheduler (scheduler=null among the overrides) and trains every step at the recipe's peak rate: the rate of the optimizer (with the per-group multipliers of ParamGroups), or max_lr for OneCycleLR and CyclicLR. When the probe's batches hold fewer frames than the recipe's, that peak is scaled by their ratio (the linear scaling rule; FineGrasp's 0.008 for batches of 32 becomes 0.002 on the 8 frames of a grid probe), and a note says so. A batch-norm momentum that the recipe decays per epoch (BNMomentumHook of GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp and HGGD) is held at its first epoch's value the same way (hooks.<i>.decay=1 among the overrides, and a note): decayed over epochs of a few iterations it reaches its floor of 0.001 within the probe, and the running statistics that prediction normalises with stop following the weights (Scale-Balanced-Grasp then predicted no grasp after 250 iterations). The optimizer with its weight decay, the clipping, the accumulation and every other hook stay the recipe's, and the config hash does not change. In place of the line lr the probe prints schedule constant: 0.001, the recipe's peak rate, at every step. The default, --schedule recipe, runs the recipe as shipped; the measured grid probes with constant.

A probe is one run, and it does not repeat. Run the command again and the hash, the parameter count and the first column of losses are the same (the first losses to about six digits); the last column, the seed fractions and the grasp counts are not. Training on a GPU is not bit-reproducible here, and after the first optimizer step two runs are two trajectories. Two probes of the shipped GSNet config on one machine: total loss 17.43 at the first iteration both times, 1.89 and 1.72 at the last; 233 and 279 grasps on the two frames, then 164 and 188; the smallest fraction of real seeds 0.65, then 0.68. The probe shown above predicted 1024 grasps on both frames in the run just before it. So read the numbers as "of this run", and a verdict on the edge the same way: see The verdict.

Line What it tells you losses Every loss term at the first and the last iteration, then its fall: from its first active value (reported and not exactly 0) to the mean of the last quarter of its active iterations, and its flags: flat (moved less than 5 %), rising (the last half of the active iterations more than 10 % above the first half), zero at end (0 or missing at the last iteration), constant (the very same value every time). A grasp term that is 0 until a seed is supervised starts where it becomes active, and the line says in how many iterations it was. Falling on eight frames means the stages and the labels fit together, nothing more; --json has every iteration's value. seeds, real The fraction of seed slots that held a real seed. Below 1 the proposal let fewer points through than it has seeds; at 0 an iteration trained the proposal only. seeds, supervised The fraction of seeds that took part in the grasp losses: 1 for GSNet by construction, about a tenth for EconomicGrasp with an untrained proposal (a seed counts only within 5 mm of a label point), about half for GraspNet-baseline (seeds on an object). predicted Grasps per frame. A model trained for twenty iterations often predicts few, and the count changes from run to run. When no frame has a grasp the verdict is runs-empty: every stage ran, and the detector dropped the grasps of seeds that are not valid (no point passed the proposal, or the view stage classified the seed as background) or below its score threshold, at the very end. scores The smallest, the median and the largest score of the grasps of each predicted frame, in the detector's own score unit. gradient The units of the model that never received a gradient (an L2 norm above 1e-8) before an optimizer step: sub-modules at depth 2, such as backbone.encoder or head.score_net, and parameters a top-level part holds itself. A top-level part none of whose units was reached is named alone and makes the run runs-unstable (a dead stage); a unit inside a part that learned is reported, not judged. changed The top-level parts whose trainable weights did not change between before the first optimizer step and after the last one (a relative change of at most 1e-6). A frozen encoder is expected here; a stage that should learn is not. lr The learning rate of the first optimizer at the first and at the last step, and their ratio. A schedule that steps per epoch decays with the epochs of the probe, which follow from the batch size and the eight frames: under GSNet's recipe, 0.95 per epoch at 2 iterations per epoch, the last of 20 steps runs at 0.95⁹ = 0.63 of the first rate. With --schedule constant the line is schedule and names the one rate every step used. trained, memory Seconds per iteration and peak GPU memory of this process, on this machine at this moment.

docs.title: The verdict
docs.text:
A probe ends with exactly one of six verdicts.

Verdict Meaning Exit status runs On real frames: the detector was built, every requested training iteration ran with finite losses and at least one real seed, every top-level part of the model that holds trainable parameters received a gradient in at least one iteration, the weights stayed finite, and prediction returned one valid grasp group for every probed frame, at least one of them with a grasp. 0 runs-empty As runs, except that no probed frame has a grasp: prediction returned one valid grasp group for every probed frame and every group is empty. Every stage ran; a model trained for a few iterations often keeps no seed. A run that is also unstable is runs-unstable. 0 runs-unstable On real frames: the detector was built, trained and predicted, but a loss or a weight became non-finite (a non-finite loss ends the training there), or an iteration had no real seed (no scene point passed the proposal, so only the proposal was trained), or no iteration supervised a seed, or a top-level part with trainable parameters received no gradient in any iteration, or fewer iterations ran or fewer frames were predicted than were asked for. 1 fails An exception was raised after the config check had passed. The report names the phase (build, data, optimizer, loss, backward, step, hook, predict), the component it came from and the message. 1 refused The config check refused the config (the same check as grasppanda print-config --check --for train). Nothing was built; the report carries the messages. 2 wired No real frame was read. On a synthetic table-top scene with random labels the detector was built, back-propagated a loss through every stage and predicted. This shows that the stages connect; it says nothing about real data. 0 with --synthetic, else 3

runs-unstable is what an untuned recipe looks like. A deep encoder under a learning rate chosen for a shallow one can lose every seed for a few iterations and recover; the verdict says which iterations, and the combination still works in the sense of this page. Because a probe is one run and the seed fractions differ between runs, a combination near that edge can be runs in one probe and runs-unstable in the next. Treat the two verdicts as one answer, "it works", and the difference as a hint to watch metric/real_seeds when you train.

runs-empty is common for a method that keeps only grasps above a score threshold: after twenty iterations no seed may pass it yet (GSNet with the PointNeXt encoder predicts no grasp on either frame of its probe). It ran every stage, so it works in the sense of this page too; train longer before you read anything into it.
